source.title: Lifting and automorphy of reducible mod p Galois representations over global fields
source.authors: Najmuddin Fakhruddin, Chandrashekhar Khare, Stefan Patrikis

summary: The paper proves a lifting theorem for G-valued residual representations ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) of global fields, reducible ones included (Theorem 5.2 = Theorem E): under Assumptions 3.1, 4.1, 5.1 (vanishing of H¹(Gal(K/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*), H⁰ conditions, no common subquotients of ρ̄(𝔤^der) and ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*, local lifts) and oddness over totally real F, ρ̄ has a geometric lift with image containing Ĝ^der(O′) and prescribed local components. The method refines the authors' earlier relative deformation theory (FKP19) with a new doubling argument built on cyclic submodules and auxiliary primes t_b, t_0, so ρ̄(𝔤^der) need not be semisimple; §6 treats residually split ρ̄. Applications: every odd reducible ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k), p ≥ 3, with χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{−1} arises from a newform — the actual ρ̄, not its semisimplification (Theorem 7.4 = Theorem B, via Skinner–Wiles and Pan); automorphy of many reducible GL_n-valued ρ̄ over function fields via L. Lafforgue (Theorem 8.1, Corollaries 8.3 = Theorem C, 8.4); GSp_2n compatible systems (Proposition 9.1); group-theoretic criteria (Appendix A) and ordinary components of G-valued deformation rings (Appendix B). Nothing in the atlas plans Ramakrishna-style lifting, so the global theory and its applications become a Part II of GlobalGaloisDeformations; the G-valued local material is a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings (R08.2, R08.6, L7), function-field duality a source of ArithmeticGaloisDuality, the BLGGT14 inputs a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2, and the Allen–Newton–Thorne inputs join the proposed PolarizedAutomorphyLifting. Seven misprints are recorded. After review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): 119 items (13 planned, 106 missing), 5 routes, all accepted. E1–E7 are confirmed and E8–E44 are new. Theorems 5.2 (= E) and 7.4 (= B) and Corollary 8.3 (= C) stand, with routine repairs to proof steps (E12, E16, E17, E28, E31, E39). The stated results that need correcting are elsewhere: Corollary 6.6 omits oddness (E21) and an irreducibility hypothesis (E22); Remark 6.7 and Example 6.8 are wrong as printed (E23–E25); Proposition 9.1 needs its constituents irreducible over F(ζ_p) for Allen–Newton–Thorne to apply (E32); Remark 8.2's 'p ≫_n 0' is false (E30); in Appendix A, Lemmas A.9–A.11 and Examples A.16–A.17 have false clauses (E36–E41), and Lemma A.9's condition (3) must be imposed jointly, so the proof of Corollary 8.4 covers only two summands as printed (E37). Proposition 3.8 misstates its conclusion harmlessly (E13).

items.name: A residual representation arising from a newform (lattice-sensitive)
items.statement: For an odd ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k), k finite of characteristic p: ρ̄ arises from a newform f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)) (r ≥ 2) if, for E = E_{f,ι} the completion of ℚ(a_n(f)) at ι : E_f → ℚ̄_p with valuation ring O, there is a ρ_{f,ι}(Γ_ℚ)-stable lattice in E² whose integral model Γ_ℚ → GL_2(O), reduced along some O → k̄, is isomorphic to ρ̄. §7 (p. 35) calls ρ̄ : Γ_{ℚ,S} → GL_2(k) modular of weight r and level N when there are f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)), ι and an O_E-lattice inside ρ_{f,ι} with ρ̄_{f,ι} ≅ ρ̄ for some embedding O_E/m_E → k̄. The actual ρ̄, not its semisimplification, is to be matched.
items.locator: §1, p. 2 (diagram and definition); §7, p. 35 (modular of weight r and level N)
items.note: The atlas plans ρ_f (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1), lattices and reduction followed by semisimplification (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1) and Serre's statement for irreducible ρ̄, where the lattice is unique up to scaling; nothing plans the lattice-sensitive notion for residually reducible ρ_{f,ι}. Routed to the Part II's modularity layer.

items.name: Stable lattices of ρ_{f,ι} (Ribet, Serre)
items.statement: The semisimplification of the reduction of a ρ_{f,ι}(Γ_ℚ)-stable lattice in E² does not depend on the lattice. If ρ_{f,ι} is residually irreducible, the stable lattice is unique up to E^×. If ρ_{f,ι} is residually reducible, stable lattices are never unique up to scaling, but there are only finitely many up to scaling (ρ_{f,ι} being irreducible), and at least two non-isomorphic ρ̄ arise from f.
items.note: Independence of the semisimplification is planned in ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1 (Brauer–Nesbitt); the uniqueness and finiteness statements, and the existence of two non-isomorphic reductions, are not. They are the tree statements of the Bruhat–Tits item below; routed with it. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): 'at least two non-isomorphic ρ̄' holds for p odd, since χ̄_1χ̄_2 is odd and so χ̄_1 ≠ χ̄_2; the paper gives no argument for p = 2, which Theorem 7.4 does not need.

items.name: Theorem A (Hamblen–Ramakrishna 2008, Theorem 2)
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3, k finite of characteristic p, and ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k) continuous and indecomposable with ρ̄ ∼ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1). Assume (1) χ̄(c) = −1, χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{±1}, χ̄² ≠ 1; (2) ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} is either ramified, or unramified but not of the form (1 ∗; 0 1); (3) k is spanned over 𝔽_p by the values of χ̄. Then ρ̄ arises from a newform of some level N and weight r ≥ 2.
items.note: Hamblen–Ramakrishna, Amer. J. Math. 130 (2008): lift ρ̄ to an ordinary geometric ρ with Hodge–Tate weights (r − 1, 0) and apply Skinner–Wiles. The paper says (p. 3) that assumptions (1) and (3) make ad(ρ̄) multiplicity-free as an 𝔽_p[Γ_ℚ]-module, with H¹(im ρ̄, ad ρ̄) = 0; that is false when k ≠ 𝔽_p (sourceIssues E8); (2) makes the local problem at p smooth and ρ distinguished at p (p. 3). Superseded by Theorem 7.4; recorded in the Part II as the statement it improves. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the multiplicity-freeness claim the note repeated is false as literally stated (E8); the note now reports it as the paper's claim.

items.name: Conjecture D: lifting and automorphy of L-homomorphisms
items.statement: Let F be a global field of characteristic ≠ p, G′ quasi-split over F and G = ᴸG = G^∨ ⋊ Gal(F̃/F) its L-group over ℤ (F̃/F the smallest extension through which μ_{G′} factors [Bor79 §1.1]). Let S be finite, containing the primes ramified in F̃/F and, for F a number field, those above p, and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) a continuous L-homomorphism; if F is a number field assume F totally real and ρ̄ odd. Then (1) there is a lift ρ : Γ_F → G(O), unramified outside a finite set, with Zariski-dense image and, for number fields, regular Hodge–Tate cocharacters; (2) there is an L-algebraic cuspidal π of G′(𝔸_F) such that one of the Galois representations ρ_{π,ι} conjecturally attached to (π, ι) [BG14, Conj. 3.2.2] is G^0(ℚ̄_p)-conjugate to ρ. If ρ̄|_{Γ_{F̃}} is absolutely irreducible, ρ and π can be taken unramified outside S.
items.locator: §1.1, Conjecture D, pp. 4–5, footnote 1 and the remark on p = 2
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as the target the lifting theorems give evidence for (Theorems B, C, E only when p ≫_G 0). Footnote 1: for G = G^0 with Zariski-dense image, Frobenius conjugacy classes determine the representation [BHKT19 Prop. 6.4]; over function fields ρ_{π,ι} is V. Lafforgue's. For p = 2 the paper suggests oddness should mean ρ̄(c_v) lifts to an order-2 η_v ∈ G(ℤ̄_p) with dim(𝔤^der_{ℚ̄_p})^{η_v=1} = dim Flag_{G^0}; even the trivial representation over a function field (G = GL_2) is outside the methods. Routed to the Part II's register of conditional statements. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the p = 2 variant has η_v ∈ G(ℤ̄_p) (p. 5), not G(ℤ_p).

items.name: Standing hypotheses on G, O and the multiplier
items.statement: G is a smooth group scheme over ℤ_p with G^0 split reductive and π_0(G) finite étale of order prime to p, satisfying [FKP19, Assumption 2.1]: p ≠ 2 is very good for G^der and the central isogeny G^der × Z^0_{G^0} → G^0 has kernel of order prime to p (implied by p ≫_G 0). O is the ring of integers of a finite E/ℚ_p with uniformiser ϖ and residue field k; F is a global field of characteristic prime to p. For ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k), μ̄ : Γ_F → G/G^der(k) is its multiplier, and a lift μ : Γ_F → G/G^der(O) is fixed (de Rham above p for number fields); lifts are taken with multiplier μ (functors Lift^μ_ρ̄). Ĥ(O′) := ker(H(O′) → H(k′)) for a group scheme H over O and complete local O′ with residue field k′.
items.note: The atlas's global deformation theory is for GL_n and polarized groups (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04, G7, G8); the G-valued setting with disconnected G is new. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4).

items.name: Local and global Galois cohomology over global function fields
items.statement: Tate local duality [NSW00, 7.2.6] and the local Euler characteristic formula [NSW00, 7.3.1] hold for local fields of characteristic ℓ > 0 with coefficients of order prime to ℓ. For F a global field, p ≠ char F, M a finite p-primary Γ_F-module and S containing the places where M ramifies (and, for number fields, the places above p and ∞): Poitou–Tate duality and its long exact sequence [NSW00, 8.6.7, 8.6.10], the Selmer variant from the proof of [NSW00, 8.7.9], and the Greenberg–Wiles formula [NSW00, 8.7.9] hold for Γ_{F,S}.
items.note: Number-field versions are planned: the global Euler characteristic in ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3, Poitou–Tate in R02.4 and the numerical Selmer bounds in R02.6. The function-field versions are not; they belong in those layers as their equal-characteristic cases.

items.name: Čebotarev density over global fields
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension of a global field F (number field or global function field), every conjugacy class of the Galois group is the Frobenius class of a set of places of positive density; for function fields see [FJ08, §6.4].
items.note: Number fields: Tau Ceti's Chebotarev roadmap, Layer 10 (Dirichlet-density Chebotarev; Tau Ceti already has frobeniusPrimeSet and the auxiliary-prime theorem NumberField.exists_auxiliaryPrime, but not the density theorem). Function fields: FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5.

items.name: The tame quotient of a local Galois group, in both characteristics
items.statement: For a local field with residue field 𝔽 of characteristic prime to p, equal or mixed characteristic, the Galois group of the maximal tamely ramified extension with pro-p ramification index is ℤ_p ⋊ Ẑ, a generator σ of Ẑ acting by στσ^{−1} = τ^{#𝔽}; hence the analysis of local lifting rings at trivial primes [FKP19, §3] applies to function fields.
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.2 constructs tame characters and the ℓ ≠ p inertia structure for local fields of number fields; FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.3 plans ramification and inertia for positive-characteristic extensions.

items.name: Local lifting rings in equal characteristic
items.statement: For F a global function field, v a place and ρ̄ : Γ_{F_v} → G(k): the analysis of the generic fibre R^{□,μ}_ρ̄[1/ϖ] of [BG19, Theorem 3.3.3] (or [BP19, Theorem 14]) and [BG19, Lemma 3.4.1] hold, via Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem and Weil–Deligne representations; so for the Zariski closure R of an irreducible component of the generic fibre, [FKP19, Proposition 4.7] holds and R[1/ϖ] has an open dense regular subscheme (allowing [FKP19, Lemma 4.9]).
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans the GL_2 conditions away from p at places of number fields; the G-valued generic-fibre theorem of Bellovin–Gee (Algebra Number Theory 13 (2019)) and its equal-characteristic case are not planned. Routed as a source of R08.2.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: abelian extensions and the conjugation action
items.statement: Let L/F be a finite Galois extension and M/F abelian. Then Gal(L/F) acts trivially on Gal(LM/L) by the canonical action (σ·h = σ̃hσ̃^{−1} for any lift σ̃ ∈ Gal(LM/F)).
items.note: Elementary (restriction Gal(LM/L) → Gal(M/F) is injective and Gal(M/F) is abelian); used throughout without comment. Mathlib has the Galois correspondence but not this statement.

items.name: Assumption 3.1 and the fields K, F̃, K_∞
items.statement: Assume p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) continuous, unramified outside finite S (containing the places above p for number fields). Let F̃ be the smallest extension with ρ̄(Γ_{F̃}) ⊂ G^0(k), K = F(ρ̄, μ_p), and assume H¹(Gal(K/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0. Fix a lift μ of μ̄; D is the largest integer with μ_{p^D} ⊂ K; K_∞ = K(μ_{p^∞}).
items.note: Hypothesis of the doubling method.

items.name: Definition 3.2: trivial primes
items.statement: A prime w of F is trivial if ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_w}} = 1 and N(w) ≡ 1 (mod p) (hence N(w) ≡ 1 mod p^D). Decomposition groups Γ_{F_v} ↪ Γ_F are fixed at the places of S and specified whenever auxiliary trivial primes are introduced, giving meaning to φ(σ_w), φ(τ_w) for φ ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,S′}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) (Remark 3.3, [FKP19, Notation 5.1]).
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). Trivial primes and their local rings Lift^{μ,α} are [FKP19, §3].

items.name: Enlarging S to T: killing Ш¹_T(ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*)
items.statement: Enlarge S by trivial primes to T (so T∖S consists of trivial primes) with Ш¹_T(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0, hence Ш²_T(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 0. This uses Assumption 3.1: a non-zero ψ ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,S}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) has ψ|_{Γ_K} ≠ 0, so some w split in K has ψ|_{Γ_{F_w}} ≠ 0. N(w) ≡ 1 mod p^D because w splits in K; since K_ψ ∩ K_∞ is K or K(μ_{p^{D+1}}), N(w) may moreover be chosen non-trivial mod p^{D+1}.
items.note: As in [FKP19, §5]. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): N(w) ≡ 1 mod p^D comes from w being split in K; the K_ψ ∩ K_∞ dichotomy only governs the freedom mod p^{D+1}.

items.name: Lemma 3.4(1)–(3): minimal Ш for cyclic submodules
items.statement: (1) There is a finite enlargement of T by trivial primes such that for every cyclic submodule M_Z = 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·Z ⊂ ρ̄(𝔤^der) (Z ∈ 𝔤^der), dim_{𝔽_p} Ш¹_T(Γ_{F,T}, M_Z^*) equals dim Ш¹_{T_max}(Γ_{F,T}, M_Z^*), T_max = S ∪ {all trivial primes}. (3) A further enlargement gives the same for the cyclic submodules M_λ = 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·λ ⊂ ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*. Ш¹ is monotone: Ш¹_{T′}(Γ_{F,T′}, M) ⊆ Ш¹_T(Γ_{F,T}, M) for T ⊆ T′, which (1) and the killing of Ш use.
items.note: Ш¹_T(M_Z^*) is finite-dimensional and there are finitely many M_Z^* (Remark 3.5: killing Ш outright would need H¹(Gal(K/F), M_Z^*) = 0 for all cyclic quotients). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the monotonicity of Ш¹ in T, used silently, was added.

items.name: Lemma 3.4(2): one new class ramified along Z
items.statement: For T as in Lemma 3.4(1) and a trivial prime w ∉ T, let L_{w,Z} ⊂ H¹(Γ_{F_w}, M_Z) be the cocycles with φ(τ_w) ∈ 𝔽_pZ. Then 0 → H¹(Γ_{F,T}, M_Z) → H¹_{L_{w,Z}}(Γ_{F,T∪w}, M_Z) —ev_{τ_w}→ 𝔽_pZ → 0 is exact (and likewise for M_λ ⊂ ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*). (2) holds for every finite enlargement of a T satisfying (1), since minimality persists; the paper applies it with T∖t_0, T∖(t_0 ∪ {t_{b′}}_{b′∈B}) and T.
items.note: Proof: the Greenberg–Wiles formula twice, the M_Z^* terms cancelling by (1). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the persistence of (2) under enlargement, which the applications need, was added.

items.name: The auxiliary primes t_b and t_0
items.statement: Fix a k-basis {e^*_b}_{b∈B} of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*; add to T a trivial prime t_b for each b ∈ B and one more trivial prime t_0. They make the fixed fields of the auxiliary cocycles linearly disjoint, avoiding the field K′ of [FKP19, Definition 5.8]. They are added after the enlargements of Lemma 3.4 (p. 12: 'the t_{b′} and t_0 were introduced after arranging the hypotheses of the Lemma'), so that the Lemma applies with T∖t_0 and T∖(t_0 ∪ {t_b}).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the order of the enlargements, on which the later applications of Lemma 3.4 depend, was recorded.

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (first part): classes h^(v) spanning coker Ψ_T
items.statement: Let r = dim_{𝔽_p} coker(Ψ_T : H¹(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) → ⊕_{v∈T} H¹(Γ_{F_v}, ρ̄(𝔤^der))). Fix c ≥ D + 1 and a Galois L/F containing K, unramified outside T and linearly disjoint over K from K_∞ composed with any fields K_ψ, ψ ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*). Inductively for i = 1, …, r there are q_i ∈ ker((ℤ/p^c)^× → (ℤ/p^D)^×) non-trivial mod p^{D+1}, a split maximal torus T_i, a root α_i and a root vector X_{α_i} (these may depend on the g_{L/K,j} chosen for j < i) such that for any g_{L/K,i} ∈ Gal(L/K) there are a Čebotarev set C_i of trivial primes v ∉ T, each with a chosen decomposition group, with N(v) ≡ q_i (mod p^c) and σ_v ↦ g_{L/K,i}, a positive upper-density subset l_i ⊂ C_i and classes h^(v) ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T∪v}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) for v ∈ l_i such that: h^(v)|_T =: Y_i is independent of v ∈ l_i; h^(v)(τ_v) and h^(v)(τ_{t_0}) are non-zero in 𝔽_pX_{α_i}; h^(v) comes from H¹(Γ_{F,T∪v}, M_{X_{α_i}}). The Y_1, …, Y_r map to an 𝔽_p-basis of coker Ψ_T.
items.note: Modifies [FKP19, Proposition 5.9]: Poitou–Tate gives coker Ψ_T ≅ H¹(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*)^∨; induction via the Greenberg–Wiles formula and Čebotarev in L K_{ψ_i}∏K_{ω_{i,k}}(μ_{p^c})/F, with only limited freedom in q_i when K_{ψ_i} = K(μ_{p^{D+1}}). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the statement now has the inductive quantifier order of the proof: the paper's statement fixes Y_i, q_i, T_i, α_i before 'choosing a tuple g_{L/K,1}, …, g_{L/K,r}', but the proof chooses q_1, T_1, then g_1, then v_1, then (T_2, α_2, q_2), … and Y_i depends on the g's through l_i (sourceIssues E10). The choice of decomposition groups at the new primes was added.

items.name: Proposition 3.6 (second part): classes ramified along a given Z
items.statement: For c ≥ D + 1, L/F as above and non-zero Z ∈ 𝔤^der, there is q_Z ∈ ker((ℤ/p^c)^× → (ℤ/p^D)^×) non-trivial mod p^{D+1} and, for any g_{L/K,Z} ∈ Gal(L/K), a Čebotarev set C_Z of trivial primes (with decomposition groups) containing a positive upper-density l_Z and classes h^(v) ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T∪v}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)), v ∈ l_Z, with N(v) ≡ q_Z (mod p^c), σ_v ↦ g_{L/K,Z}, h^(v)|_T independent of v, h^(v)(τ_v) and h^(v)(τ_{t_0}) spanning 𝔽_pZ, and h^(v) coming from H¹(Γ_{F,T∪v}, M_Z).
items.note: The analogue of [FKP19, Lemma 5.11], rephrased without semisimplicity of ρ̄(𝔤^der) using the primes t_b and Lemma 3.4(3).

items.name: The cocycles θ_b, θ^(v)_b and η^(v)_b
items.statement: By Lemma 3.4, θ_b ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T∖(t_0∪{t_{b′}}_{b′≠b})}, 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·e^*_b) with θ_b(τ_{t_b}) = e^*_b, and for a trivial prime v ∉ T, θ^(v)_b ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,(T∖(t_0∪{t_{b′}}_{b′∈B}))∪v}, 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·e^*_b) with θ^(v)_b(τ_v) = e^*_b; set η^(v)_b = θ_b + θ^(v)_b ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,(T∪v)∖(t_0∪{t_{b′}}_{b′≠b})}, 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·e^*_b). So η^(v)_b is unramified at t_0 and at t_{b′} for b′ ≠ b, η^(v)_b(τ_v) = η^(v)_b(τ_{t_b}) = e^*_b, and η^(v)_b(Γ_K) = 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·e^*_b is generated as a module by either value.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): θ^(v)_b omits all the t_{b′} (b′ ∈ B); where η^(v)_b lives and that its image is generated by the value at τ_v or at τ_{t_b} (both used by Lemma 3.7 and Proposition 3.8) were recorded.

items.name: Lemma 3.7: linear disjointness of the fields K_{η^(v)_b}
items.statement: As the trivial prime v and b ∈ B vary, the fixed fields K_{η^(v)_b} are strongly linearly disjoint over K [FKP19, Notation 5.1], and their composite is linearly disjoint from K_∞ over K.
items.note: Proof: the image of η^(v)_b is the cyclic module generated by η^(v)_b(τ_{t_b}) (resp. τ_v), so a non-trivial intersection would ramify at t_b (resp. v); K_∞/K is unramified away from p.

items.name: Initial mod ϖ² lift and the target local lifts
items.statement: Assume that for each v ∈ S, ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} has a lift to G(O/ϖ²) with multiplier μ (as in Theorem 4.4; cf. Remark 3.5); at trivial primes such lifts exist automatically. Since Ш²_T(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 0 there is then a lift ρ_2 : Γ_{F,T} → G(O/ϖ²) with multiplier μ. Fix target local lifts (λ_w)_{w∈T} of multiplier μ as in [FKP19, Construction 5.6] (the given ones at S; unramified for w ∈ T∖S, the λ_w(σ_w) generating Ĝ^der(O/ϖ²) after enlarging T); they differ from ρ_2|_w by z_T = (z_w) ∈ ⊕_{w∈T} H¹(Γ_{F_w}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)). Only the k-linear pairings ⟨·,·⟩ : 𝔤^der × (𝔤^der)^* → k and the k-linear local Tate pairings are used, with the trivial-prime calculation of [FKP19, Lemma 3.9].
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the local liftability at S that the paper uses without stating it in §3 was added; Ш² = 0 kills only locally trivial obstructions (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: Proposition 3.8: the doubling argument mod ϖ²
items.statement: Assume local lifts at S as in the previous item. There is a finite index set N and, for each n ∈ N, a positive upper-density set l_n of trivial primes such that for any 2|N|-tuple (A_n, A′_n) of elements of Ĝ^der(O/ϖ²) there are trivial primes Q = (v_n, v′_n)_{n∈N} disjoint from T with {v_n, v′_n} ⊂ l_n and a class h ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T∪Q}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) with h|_T = z_T and, for each n, a pair (T_n, α_n) such that (1 + ϖh)ρ_2(τ_{v_n}) = u_{α_n}(X_n) and (1 + ϖh)ρ_2(τ_{v′_n}) = u_{α_n}(X′_n) for non-zero α_n-root vectors X_n, X′_n (in fact X′_n = −2X_n), (1 + ϖh)ρ_2(σ_{v_n}) = A_n·z_n and (1 + ϖh)ρ_2(σ_{v′_n}) = A′_n·z′_n with z_n, z′_n ∈ Z_{G^0}(O/ϖ²) ∩ Ĝ(O/ϖ²) (determined by μ).
items.note: h = h_old − Σ_n h^(v_n) + 2Σ_n h^(v′_n) (the 'doubling method' of Khare–Larsen–Ramakrishna 2005, used by Hamblen–Ramakrishna), with a limiting argument over Čebotarev sets using Proposition 3.6 and Lemma 3.7; analogue of [FKP19, Proposition 5.12]. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the paper states the same X_n at τ_{v_n} and τ_{v′_n}, but h = h^old − Σh^(v_n) + 2Σh^(v′_n) gives −X and 2X, with X the common value of h^(v)(τ_v) (sourceIssues E13); Theorem 4.4 only needs non-trivial elements of U_{α_n}. The local-lift hypothesis at S (E12) was added.

items.name: Assumption 4.1 and Remark 4.2
items.statement: In addition to Assumption 3.1: ρ̄(𝔤^der) has no trivial submodule, and there is no surjection of 𝔽_p[Γ_F]-modules ρ̄(𝔤^der) ↠ W onto a non-zero 𝔽_p[Γ_F]-subquotient W of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*. When 𝔤^der ≠ 0 this forces κ̄ ≠ 1 (μ_p ⊄ F; q ≢ 1 mod p for a function field with constants 𝔽_q) (Remark 4.2). The second condition follows (running text after Remark 4.2) from: no k[Γ_F]-surjection ρ̄(𝔤^der)^σ ↠ V for σ ∈ Aut(k) and V a non-zero k[Γ_F]-subquotient of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): 'non-zero' was restored for W and V (the printed condition is vacuous with W = 0; (C3) on p. 43 has 'W a nonzero F_p[Γ_F]-module subquotient'; sourceIssues E27); the k-criterion is running text after Remark 4.2, and 'forces κ̄ ≠ 1' needs 𝔤^der ≠ 0.

items.name: Lemma 4.3: disjointness of K(ρ_{n−1}(𝔤^der))
items.statement: Let ρ̄ satisfy Assumption 4.1 and ρ_{n−1} : Γ_{F,T_{n−1}} → G(O/ϖ^{n−1}) a lift with T_{n−1} ⊃ T and im(ρ_{n−1}) ⊃ Ĝ^der(O/ϖ^{n−1}). Then L = K(ρ_{n−1}(𝔤^der)) is linearly disjoint over K from K_∞ composed with any fields K_ψ, ψ ∈ H¹(Γ_{F,T″}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) for any finite T″ (the proof never uses the ramification set; Theorem 4.4 applies the lemma with T′_{n−1} ⊋ T_{n−1}).
items.note: Proof: Gal(L/K) ≅ Ĝ^der(O/ϖ^{n−1}), whose abelian quotients are controlled by Assumption 4.1 and Lemma 2.1. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the lemma is used with T′_{n−1} in place of T_{n−1} (p. 21), so ψ may be ramified anywhere; the locator is p. 20 only.

items.name: Theorem 4.4: mod ϖ^n lifts with controlled ramification
items.statement: Let p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄ satisfy Assumptions 3.1 and 4.1; fix μ and, for v ∈ S, lifts ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → G(O) of multiplier μ; T as before Proposition 3.6. There are T ⊂ T_2 ⊂ T_3 ⊂ ⋯ and lifts ρ_n : Γ_{F,T_n} → G(O/ϖ^n) of multiplier μ with ρ_{n+1} ≡ ρ_n (mod ϖ^n) such that: (1) at w ∈ T_n∖S ramified in ρ_n there is a split maximal torus T_w and a root α_w ∈ Φ(G^0, T_w) with ρ_n(σ_w) ∈ T_w(O/ϖ^n), α_w(ρ_n(σ_w)) ≡ N(w) (mod ϖ^n), ρ_n|_{Γ_{F_w}} ∈ Lift^{μ,α_w}_ρ̄(O/ϖ^n), and either (a) for some s ≤ eD, ρ_s(τ_w) is a non-trivial element of U_{α_w}(O/ϖ^s) and ρ_{n′}|_{Γ_{F_w}} is Ĝ(O)-conjugate to the reduction of a fixed lift ρ_w : Γ_{F_w} → G(O) of ρ_s|_{Γ_{F_w}} (a formally smooth point of the generic fibre, as in [FKP19, Lemma 3.7]) for all n′ ≥ s, or (b) for s = eD, ρ_s|_{Γ_{F_w}} is trivial mod centre, α_w(ρ_{s+1}(σ_w)) ≡ N(w) ≢ 1 and β(ρ_{s+1}(σ_w)) ≢ 1 (mod ϖ^{s+1}) for all β ∈ Φ(G^0, T_w); (2) ρ_n|_{Γ_{F_v}} is strictly equivalent to ρ_v (mod ϖ^n) for v ∈ S; (3) ρ_n(Γ_F) ⊃ Ĝ^der(O/ϖ^n).
items.note: Proof: Proposition 3.6 with L = K(ρ_{n−1}(𝔤^der)), c = max{D + 1, ⌈n/e⌉}, the g_{L/K,i} chosen trivial for n − 1 ≤ eD and in general position mod ϖ^{eD+1} otherwise; doubling as in Proposition 3.8 and [FKP19, Theorem 5.14]. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): ρ_w lifts ρ_s|_{Γ_{F_w}}, and (T_w, α_w) and β are a split torus and roots of G^0.

items.name: Assumption 5.1
items.statement: Let p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄ satisfy Assumptions 3.1 and 4.1, with μ geometric if F is a number field. Assume H⁰(Γ_F, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0, and that for all v ∈ S there is a lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → G(O) of type μ (after enlarging O), de Rham and Hodge–Tate regular if v | p.

items.name: G-valued potentially semistable lifting rings R^{□,μ,τ,v}
items.statement: For v | p and a de Rham lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → G(O) (semistable over a finite extension by Berger), Fontaine's construction gives an inertial type τ : I_{F_v} → G(Ē) up to G^0(Ē)-conjugacy and a p-adic Hodge type v [BG19 §2.6, Definition 2.8.2]; R^{□,μ,τ,v}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}} is the quotient of the lifting ring whose E-points are the lifts of that type [Bal12, Proposition 3.0.12], and [BG19, Theorem 3.3.3] describes its generic fibre.
items.locator: §1.2, p. 6 and §5, Theorem 5.2 and its proof, pp. 23–24
items.note: Kisin's GL_n rings are planned in LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3 and L7 (any rank n); the G-valued rings of Balaji and Bellovin–Gee are not. Routed as a source of L7, where the extraction of Boxer–Calegari–Gee already sent the G-valued ordinary components. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the type is G(Ē)-valued up to G^0(Ē)-conjugacy (p. 6).

items.name: Theorem 5.2 (= Theorem E): geometric lifts of G-valued residual representations
items.statement: Let p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) satisfy Assumptions 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1; when F is a number field assume F totally real and ρ̄ odd. Fix an integer t and for each v ∈ S an irreducible component containing ρ_v of R^{□,μ}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}}[1/ϖ] (v ∤ p), resp. R^{□,μ,τ,v}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}}[1/ϖ] (v | p). Then there are a finite E′/E (with O′, k′), depending only on {ρ_v}, a finite set S̃ ⊃ S (which may be taken disjoint from a fixed finite S_0 disjoint from S) and a geometric lift ρ : Γ_{F,S̃} → G(O′) of ρ̄ such that ρ has multiplier μ, ρ(Γ_F) ⊃ Ĝ^der(O′), and for all v ∈ S, ρ|_{Γ_{F_v}} is congruent mod ϖ^t to a Ĝ(O′)-conjugate of ρ_v and lies on the specified component. (S̃ may depend on t; O′ does not.)
items.note: Proof: reduce to G^0 adjoint and a single π_0(G)-orbit of simple factors ([FKP19, Claim 6.13]); replace ρ_v by formally smooth points over O′ ([BG19, Thm 3.3.3], [FKP19, Lemma 4.9]); take M ≥ max{M_1, eD} from [FKP19, Cor. B.2]; run Theorem 4.4 to ρ_N; define the relative Selmer groups and finish as in [FKP19, Theorem 6.11] using Lemma 5.3 and Proposition 5.4. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): oddness is [FKP19, Definition 1.2] (new item 95). Two steps of the proof need repair: the application of [FKP19, Cor. B.2] to the image of Γ_F̃ (sourceIssues E16) and the choice of γ_2 in Proposition 5.4 when 𝔤^der is not simple (E17). The finishing argument is [FKP19, Theorem 6.9, Claim 6.14 and the proof of Theorem 6.11] (new item 103).

items.name: Inputs from FKP19: local structure at S and at trivial primes
items.statement: [FKP19, Proposition 4.7] (for a formally smooth point of an irreducible component R_v[1/ϖ], Selmer conditions L_{r,v}, 1 ≤ r ≤ M, with the balanced numerics of its part (3), valid mod ϖ^{n_0}); [FKP19, Lemma 4.9]; at trivial primes, the rings Lift^{μ,α} ([FKP19, Definitions 3.1, 3.4, Lemma 3.2]), the cocycle modules Z^α_r ([FKP19, Lemma 3.5]: for ρ_s trivial mod centre with q ≡ 1 (mod ϖ^s), q ≢ 1 (mod ϖ^{s+1}) and 1 ≤ s ≤ M, which is why M ≥ eD), formally smooth Steinberg-type points ([FKP19, Lemma 3.7]) and the local duality pairing ([FKP19, Lemma 3.9]); [FKP19, Construction 5.6].
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). The present paper uses these as black boxes; the Part II must plan them from FKP19 first. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the attributions were corrected: the rings Lift^{μ,α} are FKP19 Definitions 3.1, 3.4 (p. 20: 'see especially [FKP19, Definitions 3.1, 3.4] for the notation') and Lemma 3.5 gives the Selmer conditions Z^α_r, whose hypothesis s ≤ M is the reason for M ≥ eD.

items.name: Input from FKP19: Lazard's bound (Corollary B.2)
items.statement: For Γ the preimage in G^ad(O) of (Ad∘ρ̄)(Γ_{F̃}) ⊂ G^ad(k), there is M_1 such that H¹(Γ, 𝔤^der ⊗_O O/ϖ^M) → H¹(Γ, ρ̄(𝔤^der) ⊗_O k) is zero for all M ≥ M_1. [FKP19, Cor. B.2] assumes H⁰(Γ, 𝔤^der ⊗ k) = 0, i.e. ρ̄(𝔤^der)^{Γ_F̃} = 0 with F̃ the fixed field of ker(Γ_F → π_0(G)); Assumption 4.1 gives only the Γ_F-invariants, which is enough when G = G^0 (sourceIssues E16).
items.locator: §5, proof of Theorem 5.2, p. 24 (citing [FKP19, Corollary B.2])
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). Rests on Lazard's cohomology of p-adic Lie groups. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the hypothesis of [FKP19, Cor. B.2] (FKP19 p. 64) was added; see E16 for disconnected G.

items.name: Relative Selmer and dual Selmer groups; balance
items.statement: With M, N, S′ = T_N as in the proof of Theorem 5.2, the relative Selmer group, the image of H¹_{L_M}(Γ_{F,S′}, ρ_M(𝔤^der)) → H¹_{L_1}(Γ_{F,S′}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) (written with an overline), and relative dual Selmer group, the image of H¹_{L_M^⊥}(Γ_{F,S′}, ρ_M(𝔤^der)^*) → H¹_{L_1^⊥}(Γ_{F,S′}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*), of [FKP19, Definition 6.2], for Selmer conditions L_{r,v} (from [FKP19, Prop. 4.7] at S, unramified classes where ρ_N is unramified, [FKP19, Lemma 3.5] with s = eD at the new ramified primes). Their Selmer and dual Selmer groups are balanced, |H¹_{L_r}| = |H¹_{L_r^⊥}| for every 1 ≤ r ≤ M (the paper displays r = M), by the Greenberg–Wiles formula (also over function fields), and hence, since H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0, so are the relative groups [FKP19, Lemma 6.3].
items.note: FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the relative groups are images in the mod ϖ groups; 'balanced' is for every r ≤ M, and FKP19 Lemma 6.3 needs the H⁰ vanishing.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: vanishing on F*_N
items.statement: With F_r = F(ρ̄, ρ_r(𝔤^der)), F*_M = F_M(μ_{p^{M/e}}), F*_N = F_N(μ_{p^{N/e}}): the map H¹(Gal(F*_N/F), ρ_M(𝔤^der)) → H¹(Gal(F*_N/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)) is zero, and H¹(Gal(F*_N/F), ρ_M(𝔤^der)^*) = 0.
items.note: Generalises [FKP19, Lemma 6.4]; uses Lemma 2.1 and the choice of M.

items.name: Proposition 5.4: primes killing relative Selmer classes
items.statement: Assume 𝔤^der is a single π_0(G)-orbit of simple factors. Let Q ⊂ Q_N be finite ([FKP19, Definition 6.6]; new item 102) and φ ∈ H¹_{L_M}(Γ_{F,S′∪Q}, ρ_M(𝔤^der)), ψ ∈ H¹_{L_M^⊥}(Γ_{F,S′∪Q}, ρ_M(𝔤^der)^*) whose images φ̄, ψ̄ in the relative Selmer and relative dual Selmer groups are non-zero. There is v ∈ Q_N with torus and root (T, α) such that ψ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} ∉ L^{α,⊥}_{1,v} and φ|_{Γ_{F_v}} ∉ L^α_{M,v}.
items.note: Generalises [FKP19, Proposition 6.8]: γ_1 with ρ_N(γ_1) generic and κ(γ_1) ≡ 1 mod ϖ^M but not mod ϖ^{M+1}; Čebotarev for γ_2^rγ_1, r ∈ {0, 1, 2}. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the hypotheses and the first conclusion concern the relative classes φ̄ ≠ 0, ψ̄ ≠ 0 (p. 25, with footnote 8: 'These are the relative Selmer and dual Selmer groups'), which the proof needs to get φ|_{Γ_{F*_N}} ≠ 0 from Lemma 5.3. The choice of γ_2 in the proof needs repair when 𝔤^der is not simple (sourceIssues E17).

items.name: Corollary 5.5: 𝔤^der = 𝔰𝔩_2 needs only p ≥ 3
items.statement: When 𝔤^der = 𝔰𝔩_2 the bound on p in Theorem 5.2 is p ≥ 3.
items.note: Proof: for p ≥ 3 the trace form is perfect and any non-zero (A, B) ∈ 𝔤^der × (𝔤^der)^* can be conjugated by SL_2(𝔽_p) so that A has non-zero diagonal part and B non-zero 𝔤_{−α}-component; the other uses of p ≫_G 0 are replaced by Lemma 7.1.

items.name: Theorem 5.6: finitely ramified lifts without oddness
items.statement: Let ρ̄ satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 5.2 except that F is any number field (ρ̄ not assumed totally odd) and, for v | p, ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} has a lift ρ_v of multiplier μ that is a formally smooth point of an irreducible component of R^{□,μ}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}}[1/ϖ] of dimension (1 + [F_v : ℚ_p]) dim G^der. Then for some finite S̃ ⊃ S and O′ ⊃ O, ρ̄ has a lift ρ : Γ_{F,S̃} → G(O′) with image containing Ĝ^der(O′) and ρ|_{Γ_{F_v}} ≡ a Ĝ(O′)-conjugate of ρ_v (mod ϖ^t) for v ∈ S, t the integer fixed as in Theorem 5.2.
items.note: As [FKP19, Theorem 6.21]. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): t is Theorem 5.2's integer; the statement leaves it undefined (E27).

items.name: Lemma 6.1: conjugating a lift into the Levi
items.statement: Let ρ : Γ → G(O) be continuous (Γ profinite, G connected), P a parabolic with ρ̄(Γ) ⊂ P(k), T ⊂ B ⊂ P a maximal torus and Borel determining a Levi M and P → M. There are a finite totally ramified K′/K with O′ and g ∈ G(K′) such that gρg^{−1} : Γ → G(O′) reduces to the projection of ρ̄ to M(k). If P is minimal with ρ̄(Γ) ⊂ P(k), gρg^{−1} reduces to 'the' semisimplification of ρ̄.
items.note: Conjugation by a cocharacter η(ϖ′) contracting the unipotent radical. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the proof conjugates by η(ϖ′) for a cocharacter η of the adjoint torus, which lies in T^ad(K′) and not in G(K′) unless η lifts (sourceIssues E18); the statement stands with mη or after adjoining a root of ϖ′. The proof also reuses e for the ramification index of K′/K. Semisimplification is new item 108.

items.name: Lemma 6.2: large Selmer groups from trivial primes
items.statement: Let W ≠ 0 and W′ be finite-dimensional 𝔽_p[Γ_{F,S}]-modules and W_0 ⊂ W a non-zero subspace. For every n there is a finite set T of (W ⊕ W′)-trivial primes (N(v) ≡ 1 mod p, W and W′ trivial as Γ_{F_v}-modules) with dim H¹_L(Γ_{F,S∪T}, W) > n, where L_v = 0 for v ∈ S and, for v ∈ T, L_v = homomorphisms Γ_{F_v} → W with I_v mapping into W_0.
items.note: Čebotarev and the Greenberg–Wiles formula. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): L_v is defined inside 'H¹(Γ_{F_v}, W) = Hom(Γ_{F_v}, W)', so W must be trivial at v ∈ T; the paper says only W′-trivial (E27). This is automatic in Lemma 6.3.

items.name: Lemma 6.3: making ρ̄ indecomposable inside a parabolic
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive, P ⊊ G parabolic, M ⊃ T a Levi, ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) with image in M(k), and A ⊂ P an abelian unipotent subgroup normalised by M that is a product of root subgroups; P′ = A ⋊ M. There are a finite set T of ρ̄-trivial primes and ρ̄′ : Γ_{F,S∪T} → G(k) with image in P′(k) such that im ρ̄′ ⊃ A(k), the projection of ρ̄′ to M(k) is ρ̄, ρ̄′|_{Γ_{F_v}} ≃ ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} for v ∈ S, and for v ∈ T, ρ̄′(Γ_{F_v}) ⊂ A(k) and ρ̄′(I_v) ⊂ u_α(k) for a root subgroup u_α : 𝔾_a → A.
items.note: Uses Lemma 6.2 for A(k) = ⊕ root spaces. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): lifts ρ̄′ of this shape correspond to cocycles for 1 → A(k) → P′(k) → M(k) → 1, A(k)-conjugacy to coboundaries (the proof, p. 29).

items.name: Lemma 6.4: local lifts at trivial primes for unipotent ρ̄
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive, T a maximal torus, A a commutative unipotent subgroup and u_α : 𝔾_a → A a root subgroup; F_v local with N(v) ≡ 1 (mod p) and ρ̄ : Γ_{F_v} → G(k) with ρ̄(Γ_{F_v}) ⊂ A(k), ρ̄(I_v) ⊂ u_α(k). If p ≠ 2, ρ̄ lifts to ρ : Γ_{F_v} → G(O) with trivial multiplier; multiplying ρ(σ_v) by a central z ∈ Ẑ^0(O) gives a lift of any prescribed multiplier lifting that of ρ̄.
items.note: ρ̄ is tame; take ρ(τ) = u_2 unipotent and ρ(σ) = t·u_1 with t = α^∨(x), x² = N(v) and x ≡ 1 (mod p), which uses p ≠ 2. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the multiplier and x ≡ 1 (mod p) were recorded; Corollary 6.6 needs a lift of type μ at the primes of T, which the central twist provides (sourceIssues E19). Locator corrected.

items.name: Lemma 6.5: killing H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) by a non-split extension
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive, P a parabolic with Levi M, p ≫_G 0, and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) with image in M(k), satisfying the local parts of Assumption 5.1, with H⁰(Γ_{F,S}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der. There are a finite set T of ρ̄-trivial primes and ρ̄′ : Γ_{F,S∪T} → G(k) with image in P(k), projection to M(k) isomorphic to ρ̄, satisfying the local hypotheses of Assumption 5.1, and with H⁰(Γ_{F,S∪T}, ρ̄′(𝔤^der)) = 0.
items.note: Lemma A.7 (applied to G^der) gives A; then Lemmas 6.3 and 6.4. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the proof does not invoke Lemma 6.4 at the primes of T (E19), and 'since ρ̄′ projects to ρ̄' only gives H⁰(ρ̄′(𝔤^der)) ⊂ (𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der) ⊕ 𝔲; the containment holds because A(k) ⊂ ρ̄′(Γ_{F(ρ̄, μ_p)}) (sourceIssues E20).

items.name: Corollary 6.6: lifts of residually Levi-valued ρ̄ with Zariski-dense image
items.statement: Let G be connected reductive, P a parabolic with Levi M, ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → G(k) with image in M(k). Assume p ≫_G 0; if F is a number field, that ρ̄ is odd (so F is totally real); the local parts of Assumption 5.1; H⁰(Γ_{F,S}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der; H⁰(Γ_{F,S}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0; and either μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) or (P maximal and ρ̄ : Γ_F → M(k) absolutely irreducible) ρ̄ satisfies condition (2) of Lemma A.14; choose μ as in Assumption 5.1. Then there are E′/E, S̃ ⊃ S (adding trivial primes) and a geometric lift ρ : Γ_{F,S̃} → G(O′) of ρ̄ with multiplier μ and ρ(Γ_F) ∩ G^der(O′) Zariski-dense in G^der.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 6.5 gives ρ̄′; Lemmas A.5/A.14 and the hypotheses give Assumptions 3.1, 4.1, 5.1 for ρ̄′; Theorem 5.2 lifts ρ̄′; Lemma 6.1 returns to ρ̄. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): two hypotheses the paper omits were added. Oddness: the proof applies Theorem 5.2, which requires it, and without it the corollary would lift even χ_1 ⊕ χ_2 : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k) (sourceIssues E21); ρ̄′ is then odd because H¹(Γ_{F_v}, A(k)) = 0 for v | ∞ and p odd. Absolute M-irreducibility: a standing hypothesis of Lemma A.14 not implied by the H⁰ condition (E22). The H⁰(ρ̄′(𝔤^der)^*) step of the proof needs the argument of E20. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): locator corrected.

items.name: Remark 6.7: representations valued in a torus
items.statement: If M is a maximal torus and β∘ρ̄ ≠ 1 for every root β (which follows from 'the image of ρ̄ lies in no proper subtorus' when every root is primitive in X^*(T), e.g. for GL_n or G adjoint), the H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) condition of Corollary 6.6 holds; H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0 if κ̄^{−1} does not occur in 𝔤^der, and Lemma A.18(3) gives (C3) and (C4), i.e. Assumption 3.1 and the second part of Assumption 4.1: so torus-valued ρ̄ have irreducible geometric lifts under simple conditions. Lemma A.11 gives maximal-parabolic examples.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the printed claim that 'no proper subtorus' suffices is false for SL_2 with ρ̄ = diag(χ, χ^{−1}), χ quadratic (sourceIssues E23); Lemma A.18(3) gives (C3) and (C4), not Assumption 4.1. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): locator corrected.

items.name: Example 6.8: GSp_4 with residual image in the Siegel Levi
items.statement: F = ℚ, G = GSp_4, P the Siegel parabolic (Levi quotient GL_2 × 𝔾_m); ρ̄ = (ρ̄_f, δ) with ρ̄_f absolutely irreducible from a newform on Γ_0(N) of weight r ≥ 2 and δ odd, lifted with δ̃ de Rham of weight w ∉ {0, r − 1, 2r − 2} so that the lift is Hodge–Tate regular. The paper's conditions: if ρ̄_f is not dihedral (or, in the dihedral case, κ̄^{r−1} has order > 2 and κ̄^r, κ̄^{r−2} have order > 2), properties (a), (b) of Lemma A.11(2) hold; if the κ̄^{a(r−1)+1} have order ≥ 5 for |a| ≤ 2, condition (2) of Lemma A.14 holds and hence (C3) and (C4) (Example A.16); 𝔲⁺ ≅ Sym²(ρ̄_f) ⊗ δ^{−1} has no invariants except for at most three δ in the dihedral case. Conclusion: ρ̄ has a regular geometric lift ρ : Γ_ℚ → GSp_4(O′) with ρ(Γ_ℚ) ∩ Sp_4(O′) Zariski-dense in Sp_4. As printed these conditions do not suffice: in the dihedral case H⁰(ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) ≠ 0 when δκ̄^{−1} or δ^{−1}κ̄^{−1} occurs in Sym²ρ̄_f or Sym²ρ̄_f^∨ (e.g. δ = ε_Kκ̄^r), and the Lemma A.14 criterion must use χ = κ̄^{r−1}δ^{−1}, i.e. (κ̄^{r−1}δ^{−1})^aκ̄ of order ≥ 5 for |a| ≤ 2.
items.note: For fixed r > 2 the order conditions hold for all p ≫ 0. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the statement records the paper's conditions and the two corrections they need (sourceIssues E24, E25), with the weight of δ̃ (E26); 'properties (1) and (2) of Lemma A.14' is condition (2). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): locator corrected.

items.name: Lemma 7.1: the reducible GL_2 hypotheses
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → GL_2(k) (F totally real) with ρ̄ ∼ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1), χ̄(c_v) = −1 for all v | ∞, χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{−1}, and non-trivial extension class ∗. Then Assumptions 3.1, 4.1 and the first item of Assumption 5.1 hold for ρ̄.
items.note: Proof: the only lines in ρ̄(𝔤^der) and ρ̄(𝔤^der)^* ≅ ρ̄(𝔤^der)(1) are k(χ̄) and k(χ̄κ̄); for χ̄ ≠ κ̄, H¹(Gal(K/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) reduces to Hom_{Gal(K_0/F)}(P, k(ψ)) for ψ ∈ {χ̄^{−1}κ̄, κ̄, χ̄κ̄}, P the p-Sylow subgroup, K_0 = F(χ̄, μ_p), and P ≅ ⊕𝔽_p(χ̄); the case χ̄ = κ̄ is a cocycle computation on the filtration F_2 ⊂ F_1 ⊂ F_0 = ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*. Two misprints on p. 32 (source issues E1, E2). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the 'p ≫_G 0' of Assumption 3.1 is supplied for 𝔰𝔩_2 by Corollary 5.5 (p ≥ 3), not by Lemma 7.1; the whole proof was re-derived and is correct apart from E1, E2.

items.name: Lemma 7.2(1): local lifts away from p with given determinant
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3, ρ̄ ∼ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1) on Γ_{F,S}, and μ : Γ_{F,S} → O^× a geometric lift of det ρ̄ = χ̄ of the form κ^{r−1}χ_0 (r ≥ 2, χ_0 of finite order). After enlarging O, for v ∈ S not above p there is a lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → GL_2(O′) of ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} with determinant μ.
items.note: Proof: [Dia97] and [Tay03, §1, E3] (formally smooth components), with square roots of characters. LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans the conditions away from p; the existence of such lifts for reducible ρ̄ with prescribed determinant belongs there.

items.name: Lemma 7.2(2): ordinary potentially crystalline lifts at p
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 7.2(1), for v | p there is an ordinary potentially crystalline lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → GL_2(O′) of ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r − 1} and determinant μ; and there is always an ordinary potentially crystalline lift with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r − 1} having a non-trivial unramified quotient, possibly without det ρ_v = μ. (A lift ρ_v of ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} is called ordinary when it is F′_v-ordinary, for some F′_v, in the sense of Definition B.2; the paper applies the word to ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} itself, sourceIssues E29.)
items.note: Proof: [BLGG12, Lemma 6.1.6] extended to general r, distinguishing peu and très ramifiée extensions. Routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6 (local statements for the global arguments). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): Definition B.2 applies to lifts, not to the residual representation.

items.name: Lemma 7.2(3): a crystalline lift in Serre's weight
items.statement: When F = ℚ (or F is split at all places above p) and r = k(ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}}) is Serre's weight [Ser87, §2.3], there is a crystalline lift ρ_p : Γ_{ℚ_p} → GL_2(O′) of ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r − 1}. When needed (proof of Theorem 7.4) the lift is moreover ordinary with an unramified quotient, which the argument of (2) provides.
items.note: Proof: [BDJ10, §3.2]. Routed as a source of R08.6. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the printed bullet gives only a crystalline lift; the ordinarity used in Theorem 7.4 was added.

items.name: Serre's weight k(ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}})
items.statement: The weight attached to ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} by Serre's recipe [Ser87, §2.3], including the reducible local cases.
items.note: AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.4 plans Serre's full piecewise recipe, including reducible local representations.

items.name: Lemma 7.3: the semisimplification of an odd ρ̄ is modular
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : Γ_{ℚ,S} → GL_2(k) be continuous and odd. Then ρ̄^{ss} is isomorphic to the semisimplification of a residual representation arising from ρ_{f,ι} for a newform f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)), some N ≥ 1, r ≥ 2.
items.note: Irreducible case: Serre's conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger), planned in ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6. Reducible case (folklore, [SW99, §3.4]): an Eisenstein series E_r ∈ M_r(Γ_1(N)) (N divisible by a prime q ≡ 1 mod p) whose constant terms vanish mod ℘ is congruent to a newform; or use the reduction of an Eisenstein series and Θ^{p−1}-type arguments. Not planned; routed to the Part II's modularity layer.

items.name: Skinner–Wiles: modularity of residually reducible ordinary representations
items.statement: [SW99, main theorem]: an odd irreducible p-adic ρ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(O), unramified outside finitely many primes, ordinary at p with residual semisimplification 1 ⊕ χ̄ and χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} ≠ 1 (in the form the proof of Theorem 7.4 arranges: ρ|_{I_{ℚ_p}} ∼ (∗ ∗; 0 1), and det ρ = κ^{r−1} times a character of finite order, r ≥ 2), arises from a newform. [SW99, Theorems A, B] give analogues over certain totally real fields (Remark 7.5).
items.locator: §7, proof of Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5, pp. 35–36 (cited)
items.note: OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.5 plans the Skinner–Wiles residually reducible ordinary results. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the hypotheses were made explicit from the proof of Theorem 7.4; [SW99] itself was not read by the review.

items.name: Pan: the residually reducible Fontaine–Mazur theorem (ordinary case with χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} = 1)
items.statement: [Pan19]: for p odd, an odd irreducible ρ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(E), finitely ramified, de Rham at p with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, whose residual semisimplification is a sum of two characters χ̄_1 ⊕ χ̄_2 (with χ̄_1/χ̄_2|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} ≠ ω when p = 3), arises from a cuspidal eigenform up to twist; the paper uses the ordinary case χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} = 1 left open by Skinner–Wiles (Pan's §6), where the lift may be non-distinguished at p.
items.locator: §7, proof of Theorem 7.4, p. 36 (cited; named on p. 35); Pan, arXiv 1901.07166v2, Theorem 1.0.2 and §6
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting R32.4 plans Pan's residually reducible theorem (for p ≥ 5 as needed there) and R21.5 the ordinary p = 3 branch; the ordinary theorem for all odd p (Pan §6, Theorem 6.1.2) should be recorded there. Pan's Theorem 1.0.2 was read to confirm the p = 3 condition does not bite: χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_3}} = 1 ≠ ω. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the proof invokes [Pan19] on p. 36. Pan's Theorem 6.1.2 (the ordinary case) is stated for pseudo-representations over abelian totally real F in which p is unramified.

items.name: Serre's conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger)
items.statement: An odd, irreducible, continuous ρ̄ : Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) → GL_2(k) arises from a newform (of Serre's weight and level).
items.note: ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6 plans the full classical statement.

items.name: Theorem 7.4 (= Theorem B): modularity of reducible odd ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k)
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and ρ̄ : Γ_{ℚ,S} → GL_2(k) continuous with ρ̄ ∼ (χ̄ ∗; 0 1), χ̄(c) = −1 and χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{−1}. Then ρ̄ is modular; more precisely, for any r ≥ 2, ρ̄ is modular of weight r and some level; and ρ̄ is modular of weight k(ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}}) and level prime to p.
items.note: Proof (∗ ≠ 0): Lemmas 7.1, 7.2 and Corollary 5.5 give Theorem 5.2 for G = GL_2 with determinant μω, μ = κ^{r−1}[det(ρ̄)κ̄^{1−r}] and ω a local correction inflated to Γ_ℚ by local and global Kronecker–Weber (planned in Tau Ceti's ClassFieldTheory Layer 13; the inflation needs the choice of sourceIssues E28, and the construction is new item 109) and ordinary components (Lemma B.4); the lift is modular by Skinner–Wiles (χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} ≠ 1) or Pan (χ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} = 1), the weight by local–global compatibility at p (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.5). Split case: Lemma 6.3 then Theorem 5.2 and Lemma 6.1, or Lemma 7.3 and Lemma 6.1. Improves Theorem A by dropping its conditions (2), (3) and all but one exceptional χ̄. The condition χ̄ ≠ κ̄^{−1} is expected to be superfluous (Conjecture D). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the Kronecker–Weber step concerns ω, not a character χ_0; see E28 for its gap. The weight claim uses local–global compatibility at p (new item 110).

items.name: Remark 7.5: totally real fields and the role of lifting
items.statement: Since [SW99, Theorems A, B] include residually reducible modularity over certain totally real fields, the method gives mod p modularity there too; lifting reducible ρ̄ to irreducible geometric ρ (introduced in [HR08]) is at present perhaps the only route to modularity of residually reducible representations, as it was for Serre's conjecture [KW09b, KW09c].
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the paper's hedge 'perhaps' was restored.

items.name: Lemma 7.6: infinitely many extensions with the same semisimplification
items.statement: Let Γ be a finite group, L an infinite field and φ : Γ → L^×. If dim_L H¹(Γ, L(φ)) > 1 or dim_L H¹(Γ, L(φ^{−1})) > 1, there are infinitely many pairwise non-conjugate (under GL_2(L)) ρ : Γ → GL_2(L) with semisimplification id ⊕ φ.
items.note: Implicit in Berger–Klosin [BK19]. Proof: the isomorphism classes are {0} ∪ ℙ^{n−1}(L) ∪ ℙ^{m−1}(L), n = dim H¹(Γ, L(φ)), m = dim H¹(Γ, L(φ^{−1})) (the two projective spaces identified if φ = 1).

items.name: Serre's lemma: stable lattices and the Bruhat–Tits tree
items.statement: For an irreducible ρ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(E) whose residual semisimplification is 1 ⊕ χ̄ with 1 ≠ χ̄, the fixed points of ρ(Γ_ℚ) in the Bruhat–Tits tree of PGL_2(E) form a segment. If it is an edge, exactly two residual representations arise from stable lattices (the end points: non-split extensions of 1 by χ̄ and of χ̄ by 1); if it has length > 1, the split representation also arises (interior vertices). The set X_E of indecomposable reductions up to GL_2(k′)-conjugacy is in bijection with X_{E′} for finite E′/E.
items.note: [BC14, Propositions 11, 32], [Bel, §1]. ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 plans buildings and the SL_2 tree as an example, but not this Galois statement. Routed to the Part II with Proposition 7.7.

items.name: Proposition 7.7: only finitely many reducible ρ̄ at fixed weight and level
items.statement: Let Γ be a finite quotient of Γ_ℚ and χ̄ : Γ → k^× a non-trivial odd character with dim_k H¹(Γ, k(χ̄)) > 1. For fixed N ≥ 1 and r ≥ 2, only finitely many of the infinitely many non-isomorphic ρ : Γ → GL_2(k̄) with semisimplification id ⊕ χ̄ (Lemma 7.6) arise from reductions of Galois-stable lattices in ρ_{f,ι} for newforms f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)).
items.note: Proof: Serre's lemma and finiteness of dim S_r(Γ_1(N)). So minimal lifts, which the Khare–Wintenberger method produces, need not exist.

items.name: Remark 7.8: why the Khare–Wintenberger lifting method fails
items.statement: For any χ̄ : Γ_ℚ → k^×, Lemma 6.2 gives a finite quotient Γ of Γ_{ℚ,S} through which χ̄ factors with dim_k H¹(Γ, k(χ̄)) > 1. The method of [KW09a] bounds deformation rings above (R/pR finite, via some version of [dJ01, Lemma 3.15], which may fail for residually reducible ρ̄) and below (dim R > 0) and produces minimal lifts, which by Proposition 7.7 may not exist in the residually reducible case.

items.name: L. Lafforgue: Galois representations of cuspidal π of GL_n over function fields
items.statement: For a global function field F of characteristic ℓ ≠ p, ι : ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p and π cuspidal automorphic on GL_n(𝔸_F) with central character of finite order, there is ρ_{π,ι} : Γ_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) attached to π [Laf02, Théorème, p. 2; Théorème VI.1.1], and conversely every irreducible p-adic representation, unramified almost everywhere, with finite-order determinant arises (the correspondence).
items.note: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.6 plans L. Lafforgue's GL_n correspondence. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): 'p-adic', not 'ℓ-adic' (ℓ is the characteristic of F), and 'unramified almost everywhere' were restored; Lafforgue is also cited on p. 40.

items.name: Automorphic ρ̄ over a function field
items.statement: ρ̄ : Γ_F → GL_n(k) is automorphic if, after extension of scalars, it is isomorphic to the reduction ρ̄_{π,ι} : Γ_F → GL_n(O_E/m_E) of some ρ_{π,ι}-stable lattice, for π cuspidal with central character of finite order.
items.note: The lattice-sensitive notion again (not only the semisimplification).

items.name: Local lifts in equal characteristic (after Clozel–Harris–Taylor)
items.statement: For F a global function field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p and v a place, for p ≫_n 0 (the standing hypothesis of Theorem 8.1) every ρ̄ : Γ_{F_v} → GL_n(k) has a p-adic lift, as in [CHT08, Corollary 2.4.21]: §2.4.4 of loc. cit. uses only that the kernel of any surjection I_{F_v} → ℤ_p has pro-order prime to p and the structure of the maximal tame extension with p-power ramification index. Since p ∤ n, any character Γ_{F_v} → 1 + ϖO has an n-th root, so the multiplier can be matched to a global μ.
items.note: LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2 plans minimally ramified conditions at places of number fields; the equal-characteristic existence statement is not planned. Routed as a source of R08.2. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): stated under Theorem 8.1's p ≫_n 0.

items.name: Theorem 8.1: automorphy of reducible ρ̄ over function fields
items.statement: Let p ≫_n 0, F a global function field of characteristic ≠ p, and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → GL_n(k) continuous satisfying Assumptions 3.1, 4.1 and the first part of Assumption 5.1. Then ρ̄ is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: the second part of Assumption 5.1 holds automatically (local lifts above), then Theorem 5.2 gives a finitely ramified lift and L. Lafforgue (GS.6) makes it automorphic.

items.name: Remark 8.2: the absolutely irreducible case was known
items.statement: The paper claims that when ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible the hypotheses of Theorem 8.1 hold for p ≫_n 0; this is false for a bound depending only on n (sourceIssues E30), and true with a bound depending on F or under [F(ζ_p) : F] > a_{GL_n} with ρ̄|_{Γ_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible. this case is already known: for p ∤ n de Jong's conjecture [dJ01, Conj. 2.3] implies by [dJ01, Thm 3.5] (and [BHKT19, Thm 5.13] when ρ̄|_{Γ_{F𝔽̄}} is reducible) that ρ̄ has a lift unramified outside S; Gaitsgory [Gai07] proved de Jong's conjecture modulo results widely held to be straightforward adaptations (étale k[[t]]-sheaves, a complete proof of [MV07, Thm 14.1] with general coefficients).
items.note: BHKT19 Theorem 5.13 is routed by that paper's extraction to its proposed Part II GValuedDeformationsAndPotentialAutomorphy; de Jong's conjecture is not in the atlas. Recorded in the Part II's function-field application with those dependencies stated. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the claim is flagged: F = 𝔽_q(t) with q ≡ −1 (mod p) and ρ̄ induced from 𝔽_{q²}F is a counterexample for unbounded p (E30).

items.name: Corollary 8.3 (= Theorem C): maximal parabolic case over function fields
items.statement: Let p ≫_n 0, F a global function field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p, and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → GL_n(k) factoring through a maximal parabolic P with Levi quotient M ≅ GL_{n_1} × GL_{n_2}; ρ̄_M = ρ̄_1 ⊕ ρ̄_2, ordered so that ρ̄ is an extension of ρ̄_2 by ρ̄_1. Assume ρ̄_M absolutely irreducible (as an M-valued representation), ρ̄_1 ≄ ρ̄_2 ⊗ ψ̄ for ψ̄ ∈ {1, κ̄^{−1}} (automatic if n_1 ≠ n_2), and, for χ̄ = det(ρ̄_1)^{n_2/d}·det(ρ̄_2)^{−n_1/d}, d = gcd(n_1, n_2), [F(ζ_p) : F(ζ_p) ∩ F(χ̄)] > b(n_1, n_2). Then ρ̄ is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: Lemma A.14(1) gives μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) and Assumption 3.1 and the second part of 4.1; non-split case by Lemma A.11(1) and Theorem 8.1; split case by Lemma 6.5, Lemma A.11(1), Theorem 8.1 and Lemma 6.1. The κ̄-twisted case ρ̄_1 ≅ ρ̄_2 ⊗ κ̄ is not excluded but made vacuous by the third hypothesis (p. 39). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the proof needs the non-split ⇒ non-injective step (sourceIssues E31) and Lemma A.11(1) with 'n′ ≠ n″' for the printed 'n odd' (E39); with those it stands.

items.name: Corollary 8.4: direct sums over function fields
items.statement: Let p ≫_n 0 and ρ̄ = ⊕_{i=1}^r ρ̄_i : Γ_{F,S} → GL_n(k), r > 1, with (1) each ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible, (2) ρ̄_i ≄ ρ̄_j ⊗ ψ̄ for ψ̄ ∈ {1, κ̄, κ̄^{−1}}, i ≠ j, (3) [F(ζ_p) : F(ζ_p) ∩ F(χ̄_{i,j})] > b(n) for χ̄_{i,j} = det(ρ̄_i)^{n_j}·det(ρ̄_j)^{−n_i}, i ≠ j. Then ρ̄ is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: Lemma A.9, Corollary 6.6 (with Theorem 8.1's remarks) and Lafforgue. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the proof goes through Lemma A.9, whose pairwise condition (3) does not give μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) when r ≥ 3 (sourceIssues E37): the proof is complete for r = 2 only.

items.name: ι-ordinary automorphic representations and ξ-ordinary Galois representations
items.statement: π is ι-ordinary if it satisfies [Tho15, Lemma 2.3]; for K/ℚ_p finite and ξ = (ξ_τ)_τ, ξ_τ ∈ ℤ^n_+ (ξ_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ ξ_n), ρ : Γ_K → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) is ξ-ordinary if it satisfies [Tho15, Definition 2.5]: ρ is an iterated extension of characters ψ_1, …, ψ_n (upper triangular) with τ-labelled Hodge–Tate weight of ψ_i equal to ξ_{τ,n−i+1} + i − 1 (with κ of weight −1, [Tho15]'s normalisation), strictly increasing in i. Such ρ are de Rham ([Nek93, Proposition 1.28]).
items.note: The extraction of Boxer–Calegari–Gee routed 'ι-ordinary and ordinarily automorphic' to the proposed Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting; this item joins it. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the paper prints −(ξ_{τ,n−i+1} + i − 1), which decreases in i and contradicts 'strictly increasing'; the sign is dropped (sourceIssues E33).

items.name: Allen–Newton–Thorne: automorphy lifting for residually reducible representations
items.statement: [ANT20, Theorem 1.1]: let L′ be an imaginary CM field and ρ : Γ_{L′} → GL_{2n}(ℚ̄_p) continuous and semisimple with (1) ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ε^{1−2n}; (2) ρ ramified at finitely many places; (3) ρ ordinary of some weight λ; (4) ρ̄^{ss} ≅ ρ̄_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ ρ̄_d with each ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible, ρ̄_i^c ≅ ρ̄_i^∨ε^{1−2n} and ρ̄_i ≇ ρ̄_j for i ≠ j; (5) a finite place ṽ_0 ∤ p with ρ|^{ss}_{Γ_{L′_{ṽ_0}}} ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^{2n} ψε^{2n−i}, ψ unramified; (6) an ι-ordinary RACSDC π of GL_{2n}(𝔸_{L′}) with r̄_ι(π)^{ss} ≅ ρ̄^{ss} and π_{ṽ_0} an unramified twist of Steinberg; (7) L′(ζ_p) not contained in the field cut out by ad(ρ̄^{ss}), L′ ⊄ L′^+(ζ_p), each ρ̄_i|_{Γ_{L′(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible with ρ̄_i|_{Γ_{L′(ζ_p)}} ≇ ρ̄_j|_{Γ_{L′(ζ_p)}} for i ≠ j, ρ̄^{ss} primitive, and ρ̄^{ss}(Γ_{L′}) without a quotient of order p; (8) p > 3 and p ∤ 2n. Then ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π of GL_{2n}(𝔸_{L′}).
items.note: The extraction of Newton–Thorne 2021 routed the Allen–Newton–Thorne theorems to the proposed Part II PolarizedAutomorphyLifting; joins it. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): restated from [ANT20, Theorem 1.1] as the review read it (arXiv 1912.11269v2, p. 2): the base is an imaginary CM field; ρ is 'ordinary of weight λ', ι-ordinarity being a condition on π; the Steinberg place (5), (6)(c) is why §9 builds v_0; and (8) is p > 3, p ∤ 2n rather than 'p large'. Proposition 9.1's hypotheses do not give (7) (sourceIssues E32).

items.name: Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor: residual potential automorphy with a Steinberg place
items.statement: [BLGGT14, Theorem 3.1.2] applied to ρ̄ : Γ_F → GSp_{2n}(k) (the set I a singleton; ρ̄ may be reducible) with F_avoid = F(ρ̄, ζ_p): there is a Galois totally real F′/F linearly disjoint from F(ρ̄, ζ_p) and a regular algebraic self-dual cuspidal π of GL_{2n}(𝔸_{F′}) with ρ̄|_{Γ_{F′}} ≃ r̄_ι(π), π ι-ordinary of weight 0, and — adding to the Moret-Bailly argument ([BLGGT14, Prop. 3.1.1], on T_{ρ̄ × ρ̄′} over F(ζ_N)^+) the local condition v(t(P)) < 0 above v_0 — π_w an unramified twist of Steinberg for every place w of F′ above v_0 ([BLGHT11, Lemma 5.1(2)] and local–global compatibility).
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 is the atlas's potential automorphy assembly, and PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1 plans Moret-Bailly; the Steinberg-at-v_0 modification is the paper's. Routed as a source of ML.2. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): π lives on GL_{2n}(𝔸_{F′}), so the Steinberg condition is at the places above v_0 (E34).

items.name: Compatible systems from potential automorphy (BLGGT14, Theorem 5.5.1)
items.statement: The argument of [BLGGT14, Theorem 5.5.1]: a ρ that is automorphic over a suitable F′ (ρ|_{Γ_{F′}} ≅ r_ι(Π_{F′}), Π_{F′} RAESDC) belongs to a strictly pure compatible system {ρ_{ι′}} of ℓ-adic representations of Γ_F indexed by ι′ : ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ; descent from L′ = LF′ to F′ uses Gal(L′/F′)-invariance and a twist by δ_{L′/F′}.
items.note: Routed with the previous item as a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 ('track compatible systems and descent'); PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.5 supplies the compatible-system operations. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): locator corrected.

items.name: Local lifts for GSp_2n: Booher's minimally ramified lifts and Steinberg points
items.statement: For v ∤ p, ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} has a lift Γ_{F_v} → GSp_{2n}(O′) with multiplier κ^{1−2n} lying on an irreducible component of R^{□,κ^{1−2n}}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_v}} isomorphic to O′[[X_1, …, X_{dim G^der}]] ([Boo19]); at a trivial prime v_0, a lift whose Weil–Deligne representation is a twist of the Steinberg parameter is a formally smooth point of R^{□,κ^{1−2n}}_{ρ̄|Γ_{F_{v_0}}} (via [BG19]; cf. [FKP19, Lemma 3.7]).
items.note: G-valued local deformation theory away from p is not planned (R08.2 is GL_2). Routed as a source of LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2.

items.name: Dynkin: Zariski closures containing a regular unipotent
items.statement: A reductive Zariski-closed subgroup of GSp_{2n} (for example the Zariski closure of the image of a semisimple representation) containing a regular unipotent element of GL_{2n}, acting symplectically, has identity component a principal GL_2 or all of GSp_{2n} (SO_{2n} contains no regular unipotent of GL_{2n}). In a semisimple compatible system the rank of the Zariski closure of the image (indeed its formal character) is independent of ℓ; this excludes the principal GL_2 for n > 1.
items.note: Dynkin's classification of subgroups containing a regular unipotent. Not in the atlas. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): without 'reductive' the statement is false (a Borel subgroup contains a regular unipotent); the members of the BLGGT compatible systems are semisimple. The ℓ-independence of the rank (Serre; Larsen–Pink 1992), which the paper uses without citation, was made an explicit clause.

items.name: Proposition 9.1: GSp_2n compatible systems lifting reducible ρ̄
items.statement: Let F be totally real, n ≥ 1, p ≫_n 0 with [F(ζ_p) : F] > a_{GSp_{2n}} ([FKP19, Lemma A.6]), and ρ̄ : Γ_{F,S} → GSp_{2n}(k) with absolutely GSp_{2n}-irreducible restriction to Γ_{F(ζ_p)} and similitude κ̄^{1−2n}. Assume for all v | p a lift ρ_v : Γ_{F_v} → GSp_{2n}(O) with similitude κ^{1−2n} that is ordinary of some weight ξ_v ∈ (ℤ^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F_v, ℚ̄_p)} in GL_{2n} (printed (ℤ^n_+)), and that ρ̄ (in GL_{2n}) is not induced from a proper subgroup. Then there are S̃ ⊃ S, O′ ⊃ O and a geometric lift ρ : Γ_{F,S̃} → GSp_{2n}(O′) with Zariski-dense image belonging to a strictly pure compatible system ρ_ι : Γ_F → GSp_{2n}(ℚ̄_ℓ), each with Zariski-dense image. As printed, the hypotheses do not give [ANT20, Theorem 1.1(7)] when ρ̄ (in GL_{2n}) has two or more constituents (sourceIssues E32); the result holds under the further hypothesis that each GL_{2n}-constituent of ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible on Γ_{F(ζ_p)}.
items.note: Proof: [FKP19, Theorem A] (or Theorem E) with ordinary components (Lemma B.4) and a Steinberg place v_0; BLGGT14 residual potential automorphy; ANT20 over L′ = LF′; descent; BLGGT14 Theorem 5.5.1; Dynkin. Remark: [NT19, Cor. 5.2] gives essentially conjugate self-dual lifts over a CM extension, and [FKP20] discusses the Khare–Wintenberger method in GL-reducible settings. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): weight lattice corrected (E34) and the gap in the use of Allen–Newton–Thorne recorded (E32).

items.name: Properties (C1)–(C4) and the parabolic set-up
items.statement: (C1) ρ̄(𝔤^der) has no trivial submodule; (C2) ρ̄(𝔤^der)^* has no trivial submodule; (C3) there is no surjection of 𝔽_p[Γ_F]-modules ρ̄(𝔤^der) ↠ W with W ≠ 0 a subquotient of ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*; (C4) H¹(Gal(K/F), ρ̄(𝔤^der)^*) = 0, with K = F(ρ̄, μ_p) (Assumption 3.1). ρ̄ factors through P(k), P a proper parabolic of a split connected reductive G, minimal with this property; π : P → M the Levi quotient, ρ̄_M = π∘ρ̄, U the unipotent radical, 𝔲 = Lie U, U^−, 𝔲^−; {𝔲_i}, {U_i} the ascending central series.
items.note: (C1)–(C4) imply Assumptions 3.1, 4.1 and the first part of 5.1. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): K was made explicit.

items.name: Lemma A.1: a P-equivariant exponential
items.statement: If p ≫_G 0 there is a P-equivariant isomorphism of varieties exp : 𝔲 → U over k restricting to exp : 𝔲_i → U_i and inducing P-equivariant isomorphisms of algebraic groups 𝔲_{i+1}/𝔲_i → U_{i+1}/U_i; log = exp^{−1}. (Remark A.2: for GL_n, p > n suffices.)
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.1 and Remark A.2, p. 44
items.note: Characteristic zero, then spreading out from the split model over ℤ.

items.name: Lemma A.3: Jordan–Hölder for central Γ-chains of a p-group
items.statement: Let Γ act on a finite p-group Σ. For maximal chains {1} = Σ_0 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ Σ_n = Σ of normal Γ-invariant subgroups with Σ_{i+1}/Σ_i central in Σ/Σ_i (so each factor is a simple 𝔽_p[Γ]-module), the multiset of factors is independent of the chain.
items.note: [Isa09, Theorem 10.5]. Mathlib has the abstract theorem (JordanHolderLattice, CompositionSeries.jordan_holder in Mathlib/Order/JordanHolder.lean) but not this operator-group instance. One index misprint (source issue E3).

items.name: Lemma A.4: factors of the image of Γ in U are subquotients of 𝔲
items.statement: Suppose p ≫_G 0. Let Γ ⊂ P(k), Γ̄ its image in M(k) and Σ = ker(Γ → Γ̄) ⊂ U(k), with ascending central series {Σ_i}. Every irreducible Γ-subquotient of Σ_{i+1}/Σ_i is isomorphic to an 𝔽_p[Γ]-subquotient of 𝔲 (Γ acting through the natural action of P(k)).
items.note: Lemmas A.1 and A.3. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the paper says Γ, not Γ̄ (p. 44): when U is non-abelian Σ acts non-trivially on 𝔲, so 𝔲 is not a Γ̄-module. The proof's reduction to Σ = U(k) needs repair (sourceIssues E35).

items.name: Lemma A.5: μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) gives (C3) and (C4)
items.statement: If p ≫_G 0 and μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)), then (C3) and (C4) hold (even for the semisimplification of ρ̄(𝔤^der)). Whether μ_p ⊂ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) depends only on ρ̄_M (Remark A.6).
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.5 and Remark A.6, p. 45
items.note: Proof: V″ and V″ ⊗ κ̄ would both be subquotients; for (C4), [Gur99, Theorem A] (as in [FKP19, Lemma A.1]) over F′ = F(ρ̄_M, κ̄), inflation–restriction and Lemma A.4.

items.name: Guralnick: small representations are completely reducible
items.statement: [Gur99, Theorem A] (small representations are completely reducible), as the paper uses it: for p ≫_G 0 and ρ̄_M absolutely irreducible, the k[Γ_F]-modules ρ̄(𝔪′), ρ̄(𝔲), ρ̄(𝔲^−), hence ρ̄(𝔤^der)^{ss}, are semisimple, and likewise over F′ = F(ρ̄_M, κ̄) in the proof of Lemma A.5.
items.note: Group-theoretic inputs of the criteria; not in the atlas. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory, relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), no. 16, not yet extracted (a prerequisite); the paper 'does not repeat from [FKP19] any of the local theory' (§1.4). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the statement was restricted to Guralnick's theorem; the FKP19 inputs it lumped in (Lemmas A.1, A.2, A.6, with the paper's 'Corollary A.6', which is FKP19's Lemma A.6) are new item 117. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the reference list gives [Gur99] on pp. 45, 47, 48, 50.

items.name: Lemma A.7: an abelian root subgroup on which the centre of M acts faithfully
items.statement: Let G be semisimple, P a parabolic with unipotent radical U and Levi M, p ≫_G 0. There is an abelian subgroup A ⊂ U that is a product of root subgroups, normalised by M, with 𝔷(M) = Lie Z(M) acting faithfully on 𝔞 = Lie A.
items.note: Proof: a maximal abelian M-submodule 𝔞 ⊂ 𝔲 has this property (otherwise enlarge it by 𝔞′ ⊂ 𝔲_f with 2f ∉ R). Remark A.8: for L-faithful maximal parabolics (all maximal parabolics in type A; one exists for every simple G by [Sha10, App. A]) one may take A = Z(U). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): 'abelian' was added: the proof builds an abelian 𝔞, and Lemmas 6.3 and 6.5 use it.

items.name: Lemma A.9: criteria for GL_n
items.statement: Let P ⊂ GL_n be the standard parabolic for n = n_1 + ⋯ + n_r (r > 1), M = ∏GL_{n_i}, and ρ̄ with image in P(k) and projections ρ̄_i. If p ≫_n 0 and (1) each ρ̄_i is absolutely irreducible, (2) ρ̄_i ≄ ρ̄_j ⊗ ψ̄ for ψ̄ ∈ {1, κ̄, κ̄^{−1}}, i ≠ j, (3) [F(ζ_p) : F(ζ_p) ∩ F(χ̄_{i,j} : i ≠ j)] > b(n) for χ̄_{i,j} = det(ρ̄_i)^{n_j} det(ρ̄_j)^{−n_i}, then the projection 𝔭 → 𝔪 maps H⁰(Γ_F, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) injectively into 𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der (so H⁰ ⊂ 𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der when ρ̄ = ⊕ρ̄_i), and (C2), (C3), (C4) hold. The paper prints H⁰ ⊂ 𝔷(M) ∩ 𝔤^der for all ρ̄, and (3) separately for each pair i ≠ j.
items.note: Uses [FKP19, Lemma A.6] and Lemma A.5. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): two corrections (sourceIssues E36, E37). For non-split ρ̄ the invariants need not lie in 𝔷(M): ρ̄ = u·diag(a, b)·u^{−1} with u = (1 1; 0 1) has the invariant (c −2c; 0 −c). Condition (3) must be imposed jointly: for ρ̄ = ψ_0 ⊕ ψ_0^{−1}κ̄ ⊕ 1 each pair satisfies it, yet κ̄ = ψ_0·ψ_0^{−1}κ̄ puts μ_p inside F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)) and (C3) fails. For r = 2 the joint and pairwise conditions agree.

items.name: Lemma A.10: criteria for the group G_n of Clozel–Harris–Taylor
items.statement: Let G = G_n [CHT08, §2.1] (G^0 ≅ GL_n × 𝔾_m, G/G^0 ≅ ℤ/2), ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) with L/F (cut out by G/G^0) a CM extension, r̄ = ⊕_{i=1}^s r̄_i the GL_n-part of ρ̄|_{Γ_L}, μ the multiplier, p ≫_n 0. If (1) each r̄_i is absolutely irreducible, (2) r̄_i ≄ r̄_j ⊗ ψ̄ for ψ̄ ∈ {1, κ̄, κ̄^{−1}}, i ≠ j, (3) [F(ζ_p) : F(ζ_p) ∩ F(χ̄_{i,j})] > b(n) for the characters χ̄_{i,j} = det(r̄_i)^{n_j} det(r̄_j)^{−n_i} of Γ_L (jointly, as in Lemma A.9), and (4) r̄_j ≇ r̄_i^{c,∨} ⊗ μ for i ≠ j (each r̄_i polarized by itself), then (C1)–(C4) hold. Hypothesis (4) is not in the paper.
items.note: Complex conjugation acts on 𝔤_n by x ↦ −ᵗx, giving (C1) for p ≠ 2. Index misprint in (1) (source issue E4). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the paper's (C1) argument uses 'complex conjugation acts on 𝔤_n by x ↦ −ᵗx', but ρ̄(c) = (A, ν)j acts by x ↦ −Aᵗx A^{−1}; for n = s = 2, A = (0 1; 1 0) and r̄ = diag(χ, μχ^{−c}), diag(1, −1) is Γ_F-invariant (sourceIssues E38). Hypothesis (4) was added, and the χ̄_{i,j} are characters of Γ_L.

items.name: Lemma A.11: maximal parabolics with abelian unipotent radical
items.statement: Suppose [F(ζ_p) : F] ≫_G 0, P maximal and ρ̄_M absolutely irreducible, with (G, P) one of: (1) GL_n, P for n = n′ + n″ (ρ̄ an extension of ρ̄″_M by ρ̄′_M); (a) n′ ≠ n″, or ρ̄′_M ≄ ρ̄″_M; (b) n′ ≠ n″, or ρ̄′_M ≄ ρ̄″_M ⊗ κ̄^{−1}; (2) GSp_{2n}, Siegel parabolic, M ≅ GL_n × 𝔾_m via (A, ν) ↦ diag(A, νᵗA^{−1}), with ρ̄_M = (ρ̄′_M, δ), so that 𝔲 ≅ Sym²(std) ⊗ ν^{−1}: (a) ρ̄′_M preserves no non-degenerate symmetric form with multiplier δ, (b) none with multiplier δκ̄^{−1}; (3) SO_n, stabiliser of an isotropic line, M ≅ SO_{n−2} × 𝔾_m, ρ̄′_M the (n − 2)-dimensional representation given by the tensor product of the standard representations of the two factors: (a) ρ̄′_M has no invariant vector, (b) no κ̄^{±1}-invariant vector; (4) SO_{2n}, stabiliser of a maximal isotropic subspace, M ≅ GL_n: (a) ρ̄_M preserves no non-degenerate alternating form, (b) none up to scalar with multiplier κ̄. If ρ̄(Γ_F) → M(k) is not injective, (a) implies (C1) and (b) implies (C2). The paper prints 'n is odd, or n′ = n″ and …' in (1) and omits δ in (2).
items.note: Proof: (𝔤^der)^{ss} = 𝔪′ ⊕ 𝔲 ⊕ 𝔲^− semisimple by [Gur99]; the M-action on 𝔲 is λ_1 ⊗ λ_2^∨, Sym², std ⊠ std, ∧² in cases (1)–(4); centralisers of semisimple elements are connected reductive [Ste75, Theorem 3.14]. Remark A.12: similar conditions for any maximal P from [Sha10, Apps. A, B]. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): three corrections. (1): the proof never uses parity, and Corollary 8.3 needs the case n′ ≠ n″ with n even (sourceIssues E39). (2): the Levi acts on 𝔲 by X ↦ ν^{−1}AXᵗA, so the conditions involve the similitude δ, as Example 6.8's '𝔲⁺ ≅ Sym²(ρ̄_f) ⊗ δ^{−1}' does; with ρ̄_1 dihedral and δ = ε_K det ρ̄_1 the printed (a) holds but (C1) fails (E40). (3): how ρ̄′_M is defined was restored; read on the SO_{n−2}-projection alone the conditions would be wrong.

items.name: Definition A.13: property D(s, t, N)
items.statement: For P maximal, let χ : Γ_F → 𝔾_m(k) be the composite Γ_F → P(k) → M̄(k) → 𝔾_m(k) (M̄ the Levi quotient of the image of P in G^ad). ρ̄ satisfies D(s, t, N) if for all σ ∈ Aut(k), all F′/F with [F′ : F] ≤ N and all m_1, m_2 ∈ ℤ with |m_1|, |m_2| ≤ t, (χ^{m_1})^σ|_{Γ_{F′}} ≠ (χ^{m_2} ⊗ κ̄^s)|_{Γ_{F′}}.
items.note: Γ′_F printed for Γ_{F′} (source issue E5).

items.name: Lemma A.14: (C3) and (C4) for maximal parabolics
items.statement: Suppose p ≫_G 0, P maximal and ρ̄_M absolutely irreducible. There are b, s, t, N depending only on the root datum of (G, P) such that if (1) [F(κ̄) : F(κ̄) ∩ F(χ)] > b, or (2) ρ̄ satisfies D(s, t, N), then (C3) and (C4) hold; in case (1), μ_p ⊄ F(ρ̄(𝔤^der)). In the proof, L is cut out by Γ_F → M̄^ad(k) and N bounds [L ∩ F^ab : F]; s = |ker(Z(M̄) → M̄/M̄^der)|; t bounds the |e_i| with χ_i^s = χ^{e_i}. Examples A.16 and A.17 compute these constants.
items.note: Proof: case (1) via Remark A.6, [FKP19, Lemma A.6] and Lemma A.5; case (2) via the characters χ_1, …, χ_r of Z(M̄)(k) on 𝔲, [FKP19, Lemma A.6] (printed 'Corollary A.6') and inflation–restriction. Remark A.15: if χ is 𝔽_p^×-valued, σ may be ignored and (2) holds for χ = κ̄^n except for at most n_G classes mod p − 1. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the constants b, s, t, N were made explicit from the proof (p. 50); the note's citations were corrected. The proof's L′ = F(ρ̄_M, μ_p) should be F(Ad ρ̄_M, μ_p) (sourceIssues E42).

items.name: Examples A.16 and A.17: GSp_4 Siegel and GL_{2n} with blocks n + n
items.statement: GSp_4, Siegel P (M = GL_2 × 𝔾_m, M̄ = GL_2/{±1}, M̄^ad = PGL_2): N = 4, and N = 2 except in the A_4 case (N = 3) and the even dihedral case; s = 1; for ρ̄_M = (ρ̄_1, δ) in the convention (A, ν) ↦ diag(A, νᵗA^{−1}), χ = det(ρ̄_1)·δ^{−1} (the paper prints det∘ρ̄_1); if χ is 𝔽_p^×-valued, (C3), (C4) hold when χ^a ⊗ κ̄ has order ≥ 5 for |a| ≤ 2. GL_{2n}, P for 2n = n + n: one character of Z(M̄(k)) on 𝔲, s = n, N the largest abelianisation of an absolutely irreducible subgroup of PGL_n(k) × PGL_n(k); (C3), (C4) hold if for all σ ∈ Aut(k) and [F′ : F] ≤ N, (χ^{m_1})^σ|_{Γ_{F′}} ≠ (χ^{m_2} ⊗ κ̄^n)|_{Γ_{F′}} for all m_1, m_2 ∈ {−1, 0, 1} (the paper prints only m_1, m_2 = ±1).
items.locator: Appendix A.2, Examples A.16, A.17, p. 50
items.note: Dickson's classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(k). Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): two corrections. The character χ must be trivial on Z(G) = {(c, c²)}, so it is det(ρ̄_1)·δ^{−1} (sourceIssues E40). Example A.17 drops the m = 0 cases of D(n, 1, N): for n = 1 and ρ̄ = (1 ∗; 0 κ̄) the printed criterion holds but (C3) fails (E41). Also Z(M̄(k)), not Z(M(k)).

items.name: Lemma A.18: criteria for Borel-valued ρ̄
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) with im ρ̄ ⊂ B(k), p ≫_G 0; U(ρ̄) = U(k) ∩ im ρ̄, 𝔲(ρ̄) the span of log U(ρ̄), Z(𝔲(ρ̄)) its centraliser in 𝔤^der. (1) If the trivial character does not occur in Z(𝔲(ρ̄))^{ss}, (C1) holds; (2) if κ̄^{−1} does not occur, (C2) holds; (3) if σ(χ′) ≄ χ ⊗ κ̄ for all characters χ, χ′ of Γ_F on (𝔤^der)^{ss} and σ ∈ Aut(k), then (C3) and (C4) hold ((3) depends only on ρ̄_T).
items.note: Proof: Ad(exp X)(Y) = Σ ad(X)^i(Y)/i! for p ≫_G 0; U(ρ̄) is the p-Sylow of Gal(K/F); Lemma A.4. Improves Ray's Borel-valued GSp_{2g} lifting [Ray18].

items.name: Proposition B.1: Borel subgroups over a base are Zariski-locally conjugate
items.statement: [Con14, Corollary 5.2.13]: for any O-algebra A, two Borel subgroups B_1, B_2 of G_A are G-conjugate Zariski-locally on Spec A, and N_G(T_0)-conjugate if both contain T_0; N_G(B) = B over any base [Con14, Corollary 5.2.8].
items.note: Tau Ceti's ReductiveGroups roadmap plans Borel subgroups and their conjugacy (Layer 7) and the relative theory over a base (Layer 8).

items.name: The canonical torus T_G and the character χ_λ
items.statement: T_G = B/R_u(B) for any Borel B ⊂ G, canonically independent of B (G(O)-conjugacy and N_G(B) = B); fix B_0 ⊃ T_0 and identify T_G ×_O A with B_0/R_u(B_0) ×_O A. For v | p and cocharacters λ_τ : 𝔾_m → T_G (τ ∈ Hom_{ℚ_p}(F_v, E)), χ_λ : I_{F_v} → T_G(O) is χ_λ(σ) = ∏_τ λ_τ(τ(rec_v^{−1}(σ))), rec_v taking uniformisers to geometric Frobenii; λ dominant regular gives a p-adic Hodge type v_λ.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): locator corrected.

items.name: Definition B.2: F′_v-ordinary of weight λ
