items.statement: Let A be a finite local E-algebra, F′_v/F_v finite and ρ : Γ_{F_v} → G(A) continuous. ρ is F′_v-ordinary of weight λ if there is a Borel B ⊂ G_A with ρ(Γ_{F_v}) ⊂ B(A) such that, for g ∈ G(A) with gBg^{−1} = B_0, the composite Γ_{F_v} → B(A) → B_0(A) → T_G(A) equals χ_λ on I_{F′_v} (independent of g).
items.note: The G-valued generalisation of ordinarity; LocalGaloisDeformationRings L8 plans ordinary flags for GL_n (ACC+ §6.2.6).

items.name: Bellovin–Gee: G-valued potentially semistable deformation rings (Theorem A)
items.statement: [BG19, Theorem A]: the quotient R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄ of R^□_ρ̄ whose points in finite local E-algebras are the lifts potentially semistable over F′_v of p-adic Hodge type v_λ is equidimensional, every irreducible component of R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄[1/p] has dimension dim G + [F_v : ℚ_p] dim Fl_G, and it has an open dense regular subscheme.
items.note: Kisin's GL_n theorem is planned (R08.3, L7 'the Kisin dimension formula'); the G-valued form is not. Routed as a source of L7.

items.name: Lemma B.3: the ordinary flag functor is closed
items.statement: Let 𝒢 ⊂ Fl_G (on R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄-algebras) be the Borels fixed by ρ^λ_A(Γ_{F_v}) (closed; ρ^λ_A factors through B(A) for B ∈ 𝒢(A)), and 𝒢_λ ⊂ 𝒢 the B such that, Zariski-locally with gBg^{−1} = B_0, the projection of gρ^λ(σ)g^{−1} to T_G equals χ_λ(σ) for σ ∈ I_{F′_v}. Then 𝒢_λ is representable by a closed subscheme of 𝒢.
items.note: The ideal is generated by c_{β,σ} with c_{β,σ}X_β = p_β(Ad(gρ^λ(σ)g^{−1})X_β) − β(χ_λ(σ))X_β for positive β, independent of g, so it descends. Review (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the ideal generated by the c_{β,σ} for positive roots β imposes the torus condition only modulo Z(G) (for G = GL_1 there are no roots, so J̃ = 0); the generators ψ(t) − ψ(χ_λ(σ)) for ψ in a basis of X^*(T_0) must be added (sourceIssues E43). Lemma B.4 is unaffected.

items.name: The ordinary quotient R^{△λ}_ρ̄
items.statement: R^{△λ}_ρ̄ is the scheme-theoretic image of 𝒢_λ[1/p] → Spec R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄. Λ : 𝒢_λ → Spec R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄ is proper, so Spec R^{△λ}_ρ̄[1/p] is its image; closed points lift uniquely (λ regular); on completed local rings (R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄[1/p])^∧_y ↠ (R^{△λ}_ρ̄[1/p])^∧_y ↪ O^∧_{𝒢_λ[1/p],ỹ}, the last pro-representing pairs (ρ, B), which forms a subfunctor, hence the map is surjective.
items.note: Following Geraghty [Ger19] in the GL_n case.

items.name: Lemma B.4(1): the point criterion for ordinarity
items.statement: Let A be a finite local E-algebra and f : R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄ → A an O-algebra map. Then f factors through R^{△λ}_ρ̄ iff f∘ρ^λ is F′_v-ordinary of weight λ (Definition B.2).
items.note: cf. [Ger19, Lemma 3.10].

items.name: Lemma B.4(2)–(3): the ordinary locus is a union of components
items.statement: R^{△λ}_ρ̄ is a union of irreducible components of R^{□,v_λ}_ρ̄; so R^{△λ}_ρ̄[1/p] has an open dense regular subscheme and all its components have dimension dim G + [F_v : ℚ_p] dim Fl_G. With a fixed multiplier μ : Γ_{F_v} → G/G^der(O), the same holds with dim G^der in place of dim G.
items.note: Proof: at y, O^∧_{𝒢_λ[1/p],ỹ} ≅ E[[X_1, …, X_h]]/(f_1, …, f_{h′}) with h ≥ dim G + dim Fl_G[F_v : ℚ_p] + h²(Γ_{F_v}, r(𝔟_0)) and h′ = h²(Γ_{F_v}, r(𝔟_0)), from the tangent space ker(Z¹(Γ_{F_v}, r(𝔟_0)) → Z¹(I_{F′_v}, r(𝔟_0/𝔫_0))), local Euler characteristic and H²(Γ_{F_v}, r(𝔟_0/𝔫_0)) = 0 (as [Ger19, Cor. 3.6, Lemma 3.7]); semistability is automatic ([Nek93, Prop. 1.28], [Pat16, Lemma 4.8]). The extraction of Boxer–Calegari–Gee already routed this lemma to L7. Misprints on p. 55 (source issues E6, E7).

items.name: Oddness of a G-valued residual representation ([FKP19, Definition 1.2])
items.statement: For F totally real, ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) is odd if for every v | ∞, with complex conjugation c_v, dim_k ρ̄(𝔤^der)^{ρ̄(c_v) = 1} = dim Flag_{G^der}, the number of positive roots. For G = GL_2 and p odd this is det ρ̄(c_v) = −1.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 4 ('odd (see [FKP19, Definition 1.2])'); hypothesis of Conjecture D, Theorem E and Theorem 5.2; the p = 2 variant on p. 5
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported; no item defined it. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1904.02374v5, which the review read for this item.

items.name: Conventions of [FKP19, Notation 5.1]: K_ψ, strong linear disjointness, densities
items.statement: For ψ ∈ H¹(Γ_F, W) with Γ_K acting trivially on W, K_ψ is the fixed field of ψ|_{Γ_K}, and Gal(K_ψ/K) ≅ ψ(Γ_K) as 𝔽_p[Gal(K/F)]-modules. Extensions of K are strongly linearly disjoint over K when the Galois group of their composite is the product. Also: Čebotarev sets and conditions, the (upper) density of sets of primes of K and of N-tuples of primes, and specified decomposition groups at the chosen primes.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1904.02374v5, which the review read for this item.

items.name: Ramification forces linear disjointness
items.statement: Let ψ be a class valued in an 𝔽_p[Γ_F]-module on which Γ_K acts trivially, and x a prime split in K with ψ(Γ_K) = 𝔽_p[Γ_F]·ψ(τ_x). Then every Galois L′/F with L′ ∩ K_ψ ≠ K is ramified above x. Hence fields generated by classes ramified at distinct such primes are strongly linearly disjoint over K, and disjoint from K_∞.
items.locator: §1.3, pp. 7–8 ('We repeatedly exploit two techniques'); proofs of Lemma 3.7, Proposition 3.8 and Theorem 4.4
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. The paper's own argument, used implicitly each time.

items.name: Root vectors avoid proper subspaces
items.statement: For p ≫_G 0 and any proper 𝔽_p-subspace U ⊊ 𝔤^der, some root vector (for some split maximal torus) lies outside U. Hence there is a finite family of root vectors X_{α_n} with Σ_n 𝔽_p[Γ_F]X_{α_n} = 𝔤^der (Eq. (1)).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported from the proof of [FKP19, Proposition 5.9].

items.name: The cyclotomic tower over K, in both characteristics
items.statement: For p odd, Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ 1 + p^Dℤ_p (over a function field K_∞/K is a constant-field extension). Hence Gal(K(μ_{p^c})/K) ≅ ker((ℤ/p^c)^× → (ℤ/p^D)^×), and the only proper subextension of K_∞/K killed by p is K(μ_{p^{D+1}}).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Standard and implicit; the function-field case is needed too.

items.name: A global mod ϖ² lift from Ш² = 0
items.statement: If Ш²_T(Γ_{F,T}, ρ̄(𝔤^der)) = 0 and ρ̄|_{Γ_{F_v}} has a lift to G(O/ϖ²) with multiplier μ at each v ∈ T, there is a lift Γ_{F,T} → G(O/ϖ²) of ρ̄ with multiplier μ. At trivial primes the local lift is automatic: μ lifts uniquely into Ẑ^0, the isogeny Z^0 → G/G^der having degree prime to p.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Standard obstruction theory; see sourceIssues E12.

items.name: Cohomology and local duality at a trivial prime
items.statement: Let w be a trivial prime and M an 𝔽_p[Γ_{F_w}]-module with trivial action. Then H¹(Γ_{F_w}, M) ≅ M ⊕ M via φ ↦ (φ(σ_w), φ(τ_w)), unramified meaning φ(τ_w) = 0, and the local pairing is ⟨φ, ψ⟩_w = ε(⟨φ(σ_w), ψ(τ_w)⟩ − ⟨φ(τ_w), ψ(σ_w)⟩) for a fixed sign ε. Consequently dim L_{w,Z} − dim L^unr_w = 1, and L^⊥_v = {ψ unramified : ψ(σ_v) ∈ (𝔽_pX)^⊥}.
items.locator: §3, used in Lemma 3.4(2), Proposition 3.6 and Proposition 3.8; cf. [FKP19, Lemma 3.9]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Partly in item 29, which only cites [FKP19, Lemma 3.9]; the sign of sourceIssues E14 depends on it.

items.name: The auxiliary primes Q_N and their Selmer conditions L^α_{r,v} ([FKP19, Definition 6.6, Lemma 6.7])
items.statement: Q_N is the set of trivial primes v with N(v) ≡ 1 (mod ϖ^M) but not (mod ϖ^{M+1}), ρ_N unramified at v and ρ_M|_{Γ_{F_v}} trivial mod centre, a split (T, α) with ρ_N(σ_v) ∈ T(O/ϖ^N) and α(ρ_N(σ_v)) = N(v), and β(ρ_{M+1}(σ_v)) ≢ 1 (mod ϖ^{M+1}) for all roots β; it is a positive-density Čebotarev set in F*_N/F. For N ≥ 4M, the fibres of Lift^{μ,α}_{ρ_M} are stable under Z^α_{r,v}; |L^α_{r,v}| = |H⁰| = |H¹_unr|; L^α_{r,v} consists of the unramified cocycles with σ_v ↦ ker(α|_𝔱) ⊕ ⊕_β 𝔤_β together with φ^r_α; the unramified cokernel is generated by H_α (and dually).
items.locator: §5, p. 25 (defined 'as in [FKP19, Definition 6.6]' and 'as in [FKP19, Lemma 6.7]'); needed to state Proposition 5.4
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1904.02374v5, which the review read for this item.

items.name: Annihilating the relative dual Selmer group and finishing the lift ([FKP19, Theorem 6.9, Claim 6.14])
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 5.2 (after its reductions), a finite Q ⊂ Q_N kills the Q-new relative dual Selmer group; then the induction on (τ_n, ρ_{n+M}) of the proof of [FKP19, Theorem 6.11] produces the characteristic-zero lift with the local properties.
items.locator: §5, proof of Theorem 5.2, p. 24 ('finishes as in [FKP19, Theorem 6.11] (see especially the proof of Claim 6.14)')
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported; the step that finishes Theorem 5.2. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1904.02374v5, which the review read for this item.

items.name: Surjectivity mod ϖ^{N_1} suffices ([FKP19, Lemma 6.15])
items.statement: There is N_1, depending only on G and O, such that a closed subgroup of Ĝ^der(O) surjecting onto Ĝ^der(O/ϖ^{N_1}) is all of Ĝ^der(O).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1904.02374v5, which the review read for this item.

items.name: General-position torus elements ([FKP19, Lemma 5.13, Remark 5.15])
items.statement: There are t ∈ T(O/ϖ^n) in general position (β(t) ≢ 1 for all roots β at the required level) with α(t) prescribed, and the pair (T_w, α_w) may be conjugated freely.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1904.02374v5, which the review read for this item.

items.name: Reduction to G^0 adjoint and one π_0(G)-orbit ([FKP19, Claim 6.13])
items.statement: To prove Theorem 5.2 one may assume G^0 adjoint and 𝔤 = 𝔤^der a single π_0(G)-orbit of simple factors: the representations ρ̄_s attached to the orbits s still satisfy the assumptions, and lifts of the ρ̄_s assemble to a lift of ρ̄.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported. FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1904.02374v5, which the review read for this item.

items.name: The Lie-theoretic lemma behind Proposition 5.4 (proof of [FKP19, Proposition 6.8])
items.statement: For G simple and p ≫_G 0, and non-zero A ∈ 𝔤_k, B ∈ 𝔤_k^*, there is g ∈ G(k) with Ad(g)A ∉ ker(α|_𝔱) ⊕ ⊕_β 𝔤_β and Ad(g)B ∉ 𝔤_α^⊥ (by counting points in Bruhat cells).
items.locator: §5, proof of Proposition 5.4, p. 26 ('The purely Lie-theoretic part of the argument of loc. cit.'); explicit for 𝔰𝔩_2 in Corollary 5.5
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported; the core of Proposition 5.4, applied there in one simple factor (sourceIssues E17). FKP19 = Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Duke Math. J. 170 (2021), arXiv 1904.02374v5, which the review read for this item.

items.name: The semisimplification of a G-valued ρ̄ ([Ser05, Proposition 3.3])
items.statement: A semisimplification of ρ̄ : Γ → G(k) is its projection to a Levi factor of a minimal parabolic containing ρ̄(Γ); it is unique up to G(k)-conjugacy.
items.locator: §6, proof of Lemma 6.1, p. 28, and later
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. Imported. LanglandsParameterStacks LP2 plans G-complete reducibility for Langlands parameters, not this finite-field statement; the review did not check that Serre's Proposition 3.3 gives G(k)-conjugacy over a finite k.

items.name: Matching the determinant in Theorem 7.4
items.statement: With r ≥ 2 fixed, μ = κ^{r−1}·[det(ρ̄)κ̄^{1−r}]. There is a local character ω : Γ_{ℚ_p} → (O′)^× with trivial reduction such that ρ̄|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} has an ordinary potentially crystalline lift with determinant μω and an unramified quotient; ω can be chosen of finite p-power order with ω(Art(p)) = 1 (in the très ramifié case after twisting ρ_p by an extension of ψ_2|_I^{−1} trivial on Art(p); ω = 1 otherwise), and then inflated to Γ_ℚ, unramified outside p, by local and global Kronecker–Weber.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. The paper's construction, with the choice of ω its proof leaves out (sourceIssues E28).

items.name: Local–global compatibility at p for newforms
items.statement: For a newform f ∈ S_r(Γ_1(N)) and ι, ρ_{f,ι}|_{Γ_{ℚ_p}} is de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights {0, r − 1}, and crystalline when p ∤ N.
items.locator: §7, proof of Theorem 7.4, pp. 35–36 ('the claim about the weight')
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. R19.5 plans 'the de Rham/crystalline/potentially semistable statements, Hodge weights' for these representations; item 53's note already named it.

items.name: Galois representations of RACSDC automorphic representations over CM fields
items.statement: For a regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal π of GL_m(𝔸_L), L CM, and ι : ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_p, there is a continuous semisimple r_ι(π) : Γ_L → GL_m(ℚ̄_p), compatible with local Langlands at all finite places ([CH13], [Car12], [Car14]); r̄_ι(π) is the semisimplified reduction.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. AG2.2 constructs these representations for polarized cuspidal systems and AG2.6 their local properties at the coefficient prime.

items.name: Compatible systems of ℓ-adic representations ([BLGGT14, §5.1])
items.statement: A (weakly) compatible system of ℓ-adic representations of Γ_F over a number field M: representations ρ_λ : Γ_F → GL_m(\overline{M}_λ) with a common finite ramification set and common characteristic polynomials of Frobenius; strictly pure means pure of a fixed weight at every place, with Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations independent of λ.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. R24.5:operations builds 'compatible systems as actual representations … weak, almost strict and strict' and AG2.6 the weakly compatible system object.

items.name: Base change and descent between a CM field and its totally real subfield
items.statement: For L′/F′ a CM quadratic extension and Π a Gal(L′/F′)-invariant RACSDC representation of GL_m(𝔸_{L′}), Π descends to a RAESDC Π_{F′} of GL_m(𝔸_{F′}) with BC_{L′/F′}(Π_{F′}) = Π, unique up to twist by δ_{L′/F′}, and the Galois representations match.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. ML.5 registers cyclic base change and ET.7a the Arthur–Clozel base-change steps; the review of PAPER-CLOZEL-THORNE-17 planned soluble base change and descent in the same layers. Only partly in item 69.

items.name: Deligne–Serre lifting of a mod p eigenform
items.statement: A mod p cuspidal Hecke eigenform (here Θ^{p−1}(Ē)) lifts to a characteristic-zero eigenform of the same weight and level; with the Eisenstein congruence this makes the semisimplification of an odd ρ̄ modular.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. R15.5 plans 'the Deligne–Serre eigenvalue-lifting lemma for a finite Hecke algebra and its application to the relevant modular-form modules'.

items.name: The exponential and the adjoint action on 𝔲
items.statement: For p ≫_G 0, X ∈ 𝔲 and Y ∈ 𝔤: Ad(exp X)(Y) = Σ_{i≥0} ad(X)^i(Y)/i!, a finite sum. Hence [X, Y] = 0 iff Ad(exp X)(Y) = Y.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Lemma A.18, p. 51; used implicitly in Lemma 6.5
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. The paper's own.

items.name: The semisimplified adjoint representation for a parabolic
items.statement: As M(k)-modules, (𝔤^der)^{ss} ≅ 𝔪′ ⊕ 𝔲 ⊕ 𝔲^−, with 𝔪′ the Lie algebra of a Levi of the image of P in G^ad; the Killing form gives 𝔲^− ≅ 𝔲^∨. When ρ̄_M is absolutely irreducible and p ≫_G 0 each ρ̄-summand is semisimple [Gur99]. For P maximal, Z(𝔪′) is one-dimensional and equals H⁰(Γ_F, ρ̄(𝔪′)). Z(M̄) acts trivially on 𝔪′, by characters χ_1, …, χ_r on 𝔲 and by their inverses on 𝔲^−.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Lemma A.11, p. 48, reused pp. 49–50
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22. The paper's own set-up for Lemmas A.11 and A.14.

items.name: Absolutely irreducible subgroups of G(k) ([FKP19, Appendix A])
items.statement: Γ ⊂ G(k) is absolutely irreducible if it lies in no proper parabolic of G_{k̄}. [FKP19, Lemma A.1]: for p > 2(dim 𝔤^der + 1), 𝔤^der is semisimple as a Γ-module, Γ has no non-trivial normal p-subgroup, and H¹(Γ, 𝔤^der) = 0, also after twisting by a character. [FKP19, Lemma A.2]: H⁰(Γ, 𝔤^der) = 0. [FKP19, Lemma A.6]: an absolutely irreducible Γ has no cyclic quotient of order ≥ a_G (modulo the centre).

routes.title: Global Galois deformation rings, Part II: lifting G-valued residual representations over global fields, including the reducible case
routes.brief:
Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis (Invent. Math. 228 (2022)) prove that a residual representation ρ̄ : Γ_F → G(k) of a global field — G smooth over ℤ_p with split reductive G^0 and π_0(G) of order prime to p, ρ̄ possibly reducible, odd when F is a number field — has a geometric p-adic lift with image containing Ĝ^der(O′) and prescribed local components (Theorem 5.2 = Theorem E), under Assumptions 3.1, 4.1, 5.1; Appendix A gives group-theoretic criteria for them. This Part II plans Ramakrishna-style lifting — killing dual Selmer groups by auxiliary primes to produce characteristic-zero lifts without any automorphy input — which GlobalGaloisDeformations does not.

Suggested layers. (0) Foundations from FKP19 (Duke Math. J. 170 (2021)), which the paper uses as a black box and which should be extracted first, as Pan's first paper was for DESIGN-PAN: the G-valued standing hypotheses and multiplier-fixed lifting functors; trivial primes and the rings Lift^{μ,α} with their duality pairings (FKP19 §3); Selmer conditions from formally smooth points (FKP19 Prop. 4.7, Lemma 4.9); Lazard's bound (FKP19 Cor. B.2); the group theory of FKP19 Appendix A and Guralnick's theorem; FKP19's Theorem A for irreducible ρ̄. (1) Cyclic-module Galois cohomology: Lemma 2.1, killing Ш, Lemma 3.4, Proposition 3.6 (both parts), the cocycles η^(v)_b and Lemma 3.7. (2) The doubling method: the initial mod ϖ² lift, Proposition 3.8, Lemma 4.3, Theorem 4.4. (3) Relative deformation theory and Theorem 5.2: relative Selmer groups and their balance, Lemma 5.3, Proposition 5.4, Corollary 5.5, Theorem 5.6. (4) The residually split case: Lemmas 6.1–6.5, Corollary 6.6, Remark 6.7, Example 6.8. (5) Group-theoretic criteria: (C1)–(C4), Lemmas A.1–A.18, Definition A.13 and the examples. (6) Applications, each a corollary: modularity of reducible odd ρ̄ : Γ_ℚ → GL_2(k) (the lattice-sensitive notion of arising from a newform, Lemmas 7.1, 7.3, 7.6, Serre's tree lemma, Theorem 7.4 = Theorem B, Proposition 7.7, Remarks 7.5, 7.8, with Hamblen–Ramakrishna's Theorem A as the statement improved); automorphy over function fields (Theorem 8.1, Remark 8.2, Corollaries 8.3 = Theorem C and 8.4); GSp_2n compatible systems (Dynkin's theorem, Proposition 9.1); Conjecture D kept as an explicitly conditional statement.

Import, never re-plan: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3, R02.4, R02.6 (Euler characteristic, Poitou–Tate, Greenberg–Wiles; their function-field cases are routed there by this extraction); Tau Ceti's Chebotarev roadmap (Layer 10) and FunctionFieldArithmetic FA.5 for Čebotarev; ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1, R01.2 for representations, lattices and tame inertia; LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.2, R08.6 and L7 for every local lifting ring, including the G-valued rings, the ordinary components of Appendix B and the local lifts of Lemma 7.2 (routed there); Tau Ceti's ReductiveGroups Layers 7–8 for Borel subgroups over a base; ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.2 for the tree; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1, R19.5 for ρ_f and local–global compatibility at p; AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.4 for Serre's weight; OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting R21.5 (Skinner–Wiles) and GL2ModularityLifting R32.4 (Pan); ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6; GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands GS.6 (L. Lafforgue); ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 and the proposed PolarizedAutomorphyLifting for BLGGT14 and Allen–Newton–Thorne.

Final theorems, stated exactly with every hypothesis: Theorem 5.2, Theorem 5.6, Corollary 6.6, Theorem 7.4, Proposition 7.7, Theorem 8.1, Corollaries 8.3 and 8.4, Proposition 9.1. Items use the corrected statements of source issues E1–E7. Review addendum (REV-PAPER-FAKHRUDDIN-KHARE-PATRIKIS-22): the design job must use the corrected statements of source issues E8–E44 as well as E1–E7. In particular: Corollary 6.6 needs oddness and, for its Lemma A.14 alternative, absolute M-irreducibility (E21, E22); Remark 6.7 and Example 6.8 as printed are wrong (E23–E25); Lemma A.9 needs its condition (3) jointly, so Corollary 8.4's proof covers only r = 2 as printed (E36, E37); Lemma A.10 needs a polarization hypothesis (E38); Lemma A.11 must read n′ ≠ n″ in (1) and involve the similitude in (2), and Example A.16's χ is det·δ^{−1} (E39, E40); Example A.17 needs its m = 0 cases (E41); Proposition 9.1 needs each constituent absolutely irreducible over F(ζ_p) (E32); Remark 8.2's 'p ≫_n 0' is false (E30). The proof gaps E12, E16–E20, E28, E31, E35 and E43 have routine repairs recorded with them.
routes.reason: Every object here is a global Galois deformation problem — lifting functors with local conditions, Selmer and dual Selmer groups, auxiliary primes chosen by Čebotarev — which is GlobalGaloisDeformations' territory. That roadmap builds deformation rings for patching (R04.1–R04.6 for GL_2, G7 polarized, G8 determinant-variable) over number fields; it has no layer that produces a characteristic-zero lift of a given ρ̄ by annihilating dual Selmer groups, none for G-valued or disconnected G, and none over function fields. So this is new work in its direction, not a rebuild. It is not a Part II of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure or PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (automorphy lifting, which the applications consume), nor of the proposed GValuedDeformationsAndPotentialAutomorphy (Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne's function-field Part II of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands): that route proves finiteness of deformation rings from Lafforgue's automorphy (the Khare–Wintenberger method), which Remark 7.8 and Proposition 7.7 show cannot reach reducible ρ̄, whereas this method works over number fields and function fields alike. The GL_2 modularity statements are corollaries consuming R21.5 and R32.4; they stay as the Part II's final layer rather than a separate roadmap. Review: accepted. The check found no layer or candidate planning Ramakrishna-style lifting. Added: oddness, the FKP19 conventions and inputs the paper uses without statement (Notation 5.1, Q_N and L^α_{r,v}, Theorem 6.9 with Claim 6.14, Lemmas 5.13 and 6.15, Claim 6.13, the Lie-theoretic lemma, Appendix A), the paper's own implicit lemmas (ramification forces disjointness, root vectors avoid subspaces, the cyclotomic tower, the mod ϖ² lift, trivial-prime duality, the exponential, the semisimplified adjoint representation), the determinant construction of Theorem 7.4, Serre's semisimplification and Steinberg's centraliser theorem.

R08.2 constructs the conditions away from p and their components; the paper's local lifts away from p (Lemma 7.2(1), Booher's minimally ramified GSp_2n lifts, Steinberg points at trivial primes) and the equal-characteristic generic-fibre theory and local lifts (§2; §8 after Clozel–Harris–Taylor §2.4.4) are statements of that layer for G-valued and function-field places. R08.6 exports local statements for the global arguments: the ordinary potentially crystalline and Serre-weight crystalline lifts of Lemma 7.2(2), (3). L7 owns potentially semistable rings of fixed Hodge and inertial type in any rank with the Kisin dimension formula; the G-valued rings of Balaji and Bellovin–Gee (Theorem A) and Appendix B's ordinary components (canonical torus, Definition B.2, Lemma B.3, R^{△λ}, Lemma B.4) extend it, and the extraction of Boxer–Calegari–Gee already sent Lemma B.4 there. Review: accepted. The semistability criterion of Nekovář and Patrikis used in Lemma B.4 was added. Lemma B.3's ideal must include the central generators (E43).

R02.3 (global Euler characteristic), R02.4 (Poitou–Tate) and R02.6 (the numerical Selmer inequalities, i.e. Greenberg–Wiles) are planned for number fields; §2 of the paper needs them, with Tate local duality and the local Euler characteristic, for global function fields and coefficients of order prime to the characteristic. They are the equal-characteristic cases of those layers. Review: accepted.

ML.2 is the potential automorphy assembly ('track compatible systems and descent'); Proposition 9.1 uses BLGGT14 Theorem 3.1.2 (with a Steinberg place added to the Moret-Bailly conditions) and the compatible-system argument of BLGGT14 Theorem 5.5.1 in exactly that role. Review: accepted. The RACSDC Galois representations (AG2.2, AG2.6), compatible systems (R24.5:operations) and CM base change and descent (ML.5, ET.7a) that Proposition 9.1 uses are planned there and were added as planned items.
